title_zh:
他带着一台电唱机走上舞台，电唱机的放大器晶体管被隔离，然后将它们放入沸腾的矿物油中。

这就是为什么……

1954 年 5 月，在竞争对手声称耐热晶体管不可能出现后，戈登·蒂尔展示了一台电唱机和一烧杯沸油。他在俄亥俄州代顿举行的全国机载电
full_text_en:
He went on stage with a record player that had the amplifier transistors isolated and proceeded to dominate them into boiling mineral oil.

Here is why…

In May 1954, after rivals claimed heat-proof transistors were impossible, Gordon Teal displayed a record player and a beaker of boiling oil. He spoke at the National Conference on Airborne Electronics in Dayton, Ohio, where the aerospace industry faced a barrier. At the time, commercial transistors relied on germanium. Although germanium had begun replacing bulky vacuum tubes in hearing aids and radios, it failed under heat. Its narrow bandgap meant that once temperatures rose past 65°C (150°F)—conditions common in cockpits, jet engines, and experimental missiles—thermal energy flooded the crystal with loose electrons. The transistor lost its ability to regulate current, making it useless for military avionics.  

The theoretical solution was silicon, whose wider bandgap allowed operation well beyond 150°C. Yet silicon melted at 1,414°C and reacted strongly with nearly any crucible used to melt it. Throughout the conference, representatives from industry leaders such as RCA, General Electric, and Raytheon presented papers explaining why silicon transistors remained years from practical manufacture.  

Then came Gordon Teal, research director of Texas Instruments, then a relatively small Dallas firm known for geophysical oil exploration. Teal had spent months leading a quiet team to refine silicon and grow single crystals using methods he had first developed at Bell Labs.  

Teal took the podium after hearing peers repeat the impossibility of silicon. When his turn arrived, he quietly challenged them, announcing that Texas Instruments already had commercial silicon transistors in production—and that he carried several in his pocket. To support his claim, Teal showed the device on stage. He connected a standard germanium transistor into the amplifier circuit playing music from the record player, then dipped the transistor into a beaker of mineral oil heated to 150°C. The sound stopped immediately. Teal then took out the germanium unit, inserted one of his new silicon transistors, and placed it straight into the hot oil. The record kept playing through the loudspeaker without distortion.  

The display triggered a quick surge. Attendees ran to the lobby payphones to contact their corporate offices and stockbrokers. Texas Instruments representatives distributed specification sheets from the rear of the hall, securing a commercial monopoly on silicon transistors that endured for three years.

The transistor went on to change the world.

You are using a few billion right now reading this…
full_text_zh:
他带着一台电唱机走上舞台，电唱机的放大器晶体管被隔离，然后将它们放入沸腾的矿物油中。

这就是为什么……

1954 年 5 月，在竞争对手声称耐热晶体管不可能出现后，戈登·蒂尔展示了一台电唱机和一烧杯沸油。他在俄亥俄州代顿举行的全国机载电子会议上发表了讲话，当时航空航天业在该会议上面临着障碍。当时，商业晶体管依赖于锗。尽管锗已开始取代助听器和收音机中笨重的真空管，但它在高温下失效了。其窄带隙意味着，一旦温度超过 65°C (150°F)（驾驶舱、喷气发动机和实验导弹中常见的情况），热能就会充满松散电子的晶体。晶体管失去了调节电流的能力，使其对军用航空电子设备毫无用处。

理论上的解决方案是硅，其更宽的带隙允许在远高于 150°C 的温度下运行。然而，硅的熔化温度为 1,414°C，几乎与任何用于熔化它的坩埚都会发生强烈反应。在整个会议期间，来自 RCA、通用电气和雷神公司等行业领导者的代表发表了论文，解释了为什么硅晶体管距离实际制造还需要数年时间。

随后是德州仪器 (Texas Instruments) 的研究总监戈登·蒂尔 (Gordon Teal)，当时德州仪器是一家相对较小的达拉斯公司，以地球物理石油勘探而闻名。蒂尔花了几个月的时间带领一支安静的团队使用他在贝尔实验室首次开发的方法来提炼硅并生长单晶。

在听到同行重复硅的不可能性后，蒂尔登上了讲台。当轮到他的时候，他悄悄地向他们发起挑战，宣布德州仪器公司已经在生产商用硅晶体管，而且他口袋里也有几个。为了支持他的主张，蒂尔在舞台上展示了​​该设备。他将一个标准的锗晶体管连接到播放电唱机音乐的放大器电路中，然后将晶体管浸入加热至 150°C 的矿物油烧杯中。声音立刻停止了。然后，蒂尔取出锗单元，插入一个新的硅晶体管，然后将其直接放入热油中。唱片一直通过扬声器播放，没有失真。

显示屏引发了快速的激增。与会者跑到大厅的公用电话联系他们的公司办公室和股票经纪人。德州仪器 (TI) 代表在大厅后部分发规格表，确保了硅晶体管的商业垄断地位并持续了三年。

晶体管继续改变世界。

title:

A recent High Co
title_zh:
有远见的领导力是在系统漏洞影响运营之前就识别它们。

最近，高等法院就突然暂停对一家大型工业精炼厂提供企业软件支持而发生的争议，为软件供应商集中度提供了令人大开眼界的案例研究。虽然临时法院命令根据国内法指示恢复服务，但依靠司法干预不能成为公
full_text_en:
Visionary leadership is about identifying systemic vulnerabilities long before they impact operations.

A recent High Court dispute over the sudden suspension of enterprise software support to a major industrial refiner provided an eye-opening case study in software vendor concentration. While interim court orders directed the resumption of services under domestic law, relying on judicial intervention cannot be a company's only contingency plan.

For corporate leaders and CXOs, this case underscores three clear priorities:
• Review vendor lock-in and mission-critical software dependencies.
• Strengthen contractual terms regarding governing law and unilateral service suspensions.
• Foster and adopt indigenous enterprise solutions to diversify tech risk.

#VisionaryIndians #Leadership #BusinessStrategy #CorporateGovernance #RiskManagement
full_text_zh:
有远见的领导力是在系统漏洞影响运营之前就识别它们。

最近，高等法院就突然暂停对一家大型工业精炼厂提供企业软件支持而发生的争议，为软件供应商集中度提供了令人大开眼界的案例研究。虽然临时法院命令根据国内法指示恢复服务，但依靠司法干预不能成为公司唯一的应急计划。

对于企业领导者和 CXO 来说，此案例强调了三个明确的优先事项：
• 检查供应商锁定和关键任务软件依赖性。
• 加强有关管辖法律和单方面服务暂停的合同条款。
• 培育并采用本土企业解决方案以分散技术风险。

full_text_en:
Given how quickly AI is advancing, I am adding a bunch of super interesting topics to my upcoming Applied AI Cohort 6. Here's a glimpse...

1. How Claude Code Works
2. Jev and Clairic
3. Parallel, Sub, and Long-Running Agents
4. Multi-agent Task Decomposition
5. Production Issues in Multi-Agent Systems
6. Memory Write and Read Paths
7. Agent Reliability
8. Cost Efficiency

Over the last five cohorts, I have continuously refined the content based on feedback, production learnings, and countless technical discussions with participants.

With every cohort, the goal has been to make the content more practical (testimonials reflect the same), relevant, and closer to the problems engineers are solving in the real world.

The goal is simple:

"I know how to call an LLM API" -> "I can design and build production-grade AI systems."

The cohort is extremely practical. We spend very little time on slides and almost all our time reasoning about production problems, writing code, dissecting real systems, discussing trade-offs, and understanding why certain approaches fail in practice.

The focus is on building the right mental models and developing an intuition that stays useful even as models and frameworks evolve.

Cohort 6 starts on 14th November.

Curriculum, schedule, testimonials, and enrollment details are available here: https://t.co/JhtIHMrLbg
full_text_zh:
鉴于人工智能的发展速度如此之快，我正在为即将到来的应用人工智能队列 6 添加一堆超级有趣的主题。以下是一瞥……

1.Claude Code 的工作原理
2. 杰夫和克莱里克
3. 并行、子和长时间运行的代理
4. 多智能体任务分解
5. 多代理系统中的生产问题
6. 内存读写路径
7. 代理可靠性
8. 成本效益

在过去的五个小组中，我根据反馈、生产学习以及与参与者的无数技术讨论不断完善内容。

每个群体的目标都是使内容更加实用（客户评价也反映了同样的情况）、相关性，并且更接近工程师在现实世界中解决的问题。

目标很简单：

“我知道如何调用 LLM API” -> “我可以设计和构建生产级人工智能系统。”

该队列非常实用。我们花很少的时间在幻灯片上，几乎所有的时间都在推理生产问题、编写代码、剖析真实系统、讨论权衡以及理解为什么某些方法在实践中失败。

重点是建立正确的心理模型并培养即使模型和框架不断发展也仍然有用的直觉。

第 6 组于 11 月 14 日开始。

AI already writes your code.

But nobody actually checks it for flaws before it ships.

The idea?

Instead of running a pentest once a year and praying, Shannon analyzes your code, finds the attack paths, and launches real exploits against your app BEFORE someone else does.

What it does:
→ Reads your code and maps out where the weak spots are

→ Plugs into your CI/CD and fails the pipeline if it finds anything serious
→ Works with your own AI provider: Anthropic, OpenAI, local models

That means fewer vulnerabilities in production and fewer scares.

A pentest on every release, without hiring anyone.

full_text_en:
$AMD TO INVEST $1 BILLION IN $META AS COMPANIES EXPAND AI INFRASTRUCTURE PARTNERSHIP

The investment will be made through Meta's equity offering. AMD also confirmed that its first Helios rack-scale AI systems are installed at Meta and undergoing testing ahead of a broader deployment.

Meta has already deployed millions of AMD EPYC processors, including those powering its Muse AI agent, while Instinct GPUs are being used in production for AI training, ranking, and recommendation workloads.

Looking ahead, Meta plans to deploy a custom MI450-based Instinct GPU optimized for its workloads and is a lead customer for AMD's 6th Gen EPYC processors.

The companies are also expanding software collaboration across ROCm and PyTorch, building on their previously announced 6-gigawatt AMD GPU agreement.

随着各公司扩大人工智能基础设施合作伙伴关系，AMD 将向 $META 投资 10 亿美元

Meta 已经部署了数百万个 AMD EPYC 处理器，包括为其 Muse AI 代理提供支持的处理器，而 Instinct GPU 正在生产中用于 AI 训练、排名和推荐工作负载。

两家公司还在之前宣布的 6 吉瓦 AMD GPU 协议的基础上扩大 ROCm 和 PyTorch 之间的软件合作。

full_text_en:
Thank you to the news organizations making it clear, this ad has nothing to do with me. 

****

The remarks drew sharp criticism from Jewish organizations and public figures, who accused the advertisement’s creators of making Israel a scapegoat for Americans’ financial hardship and invoking antisemitic imagery about Jewish influence and money.

“Want to know what desperation looks like? Blaming the Jewish state for the price of bananas,” wrote Anti-Defamation League CEO Jonathan Greenblatt, who called the advertisement “a case study in antisemitism.”

Even Brianna Wu, one of the co-founders of Uygur’s organization, who is no longer active in it, distanced herself from the video and made clear that she would have resigned from her position had she been asked to produce such an advertisement.

Uygur rejected the accusations, arguing that his opponents were trying to portray any opposition to American funding for Israel as antisemitism. He also asked his supporters to donate so the advertisement could be broadcast more widely.

full_text_en:
🚨 $PLTR: ROSENBLATT RAISES PALANTIR PRICE TARGET TO $260 AND EXPECTS ANOTHER EARNINGS BEAT AND RAISE.

Good morning, everyone.

Rosenblatt just raised its price target on Palantir to $260 and I was going through their reasoning. There are a few things here that I completely agree with.

First, Rosenblatt believes $PLTR is heading toward another earnings beat and guidance raise. Their confidence comes from customer checks and their own analysis of Palantir's business, with estimates already sitting above Wall Street consensus.

Rosenblatt believes Palantir is uniquely positioned in the enterprise AI software market and that the shift toward large-scale AI deployments will help the company acquire more customers while maintaining strong net revenue retention.

I've been saying something similar for a while. Companies have spent enormous amounts of money experimenting with AI models. But experimenting with a model and deploying it across an actual business are two completely different things.

You need the models to interact with enterprise data, follow permissions, understand operational relationships and execute workflows without breaking existing systems. It's exactly the problem Palantir is trying to solve with AIP and its Ontology.

Companies don't need to replace their existing software to deploy Palantir. AIP can connect models and enterprise systems through a common operational layer.

Look at the numbers Rosenblatt is highlighting. 93% YOY revenue growth, 88% gross margins, 61% EBIT margins and 50% free cash flow margins.

Those profitability figures are especially interesting because they show how attractive the software economics can become when revenue scales.

Rosenblatt also believes Palantir's global addressable market is more than ten times its highest Wall Street revenue estimate of $14.6 billion for 2027.

It's a pretty aggressive assessment of how much room the company has to grow.

Palantir's biggest advantage is that it can help enterprises put any models to work inside complicated operational environments.

And as models become more capable and less differentiated, the software that connects them to real business operations will become even more valuable.
full_text_zh:
🚨 $PLTR：罗森布拉特将 Palantir 目标价提高至 260 美元，并预计盈利将进一步增长。

大家早上好。

Rosenblatt 刚刚将 Palantir 的目标价格提高到 260 美元，我正在研究他们的推理。这里有几件事我完全同意。

首先，Rosenblatt 认为 $PLTR 正在走向另一次盈利增长和指导上调。他们的信心来自于客户检查和他们自己对 Palantir 业务的分析，其估计值已经高于华尔街的共识。

Rosenblatt 认为 Palantir 在企业人工智能软件市场具有独特的地位，向大规模人工智能部署的转变将有助于该公司获得更多客户，同时保持强劲的净收入保留。

我已经说过类似的话有一段时间了。公司花费了大量资金来试验人工智能模型。但试验模型和将其部署到实际业务中是完全不同的两件事。

您需要模型与企业数据交互、遵循权限、了解操作关系并执行工作流程，而不破坏现有系统。这正是 Palantir 试图通过 AIP 及其本体来解决的问题。

公司无需更换现有软件即可部署 Palantir。 AIP 可以通过通用操作层连接模型和企业系统。

看看罗森布拉特突出显示的数字。收入同比增长 93%，毛利率达 88%，息税前利润率达 61%，自由现金流利润率达 50%。

这些盈利能力数据特别有趣，因为它们显示了当收入规模扩大时软件经济学会变得多么有吸引力。

Rosenblatt 还认为 Palantir 的全球潜在市场是其 2027 年华尔街最高收入预期（146 亿美元）的十倍以上。

这是对公司发展空间的相当积极的评估。

Palantir最大的优势是可以帮助企业在复杂的运营环境中使用任何模型。

随着模型变得更加强大且差异化越来越小，将它们与实际业务运营连接起来的软件将变得更加有价值。

Rosenblatt 将 Palantir 的目标价从 225 美元上调至 260 美元，意味着上涨 31%，理由是企业人工智能增长强劲且市场扩张。
full_text_en:
$PLTR Palantir gets higher Rosenblatt price target ahead of earnings 🐂🔮📈
Rosenblatt raised Palantir's price target to $260 from $225, implying 31% upside, citing strong enterprise AI growth and market expansion. 💥🌟💥

October 27, 2026
Investor focus on Palantir is intensifying as the software company approaches its third-quarter earnings report. Rosenblatt has lifted its price target on the stock to $260 from $225, citing expectations for continued strong growth and broader enterprise AI adoption.

Highlights
Rosenblatt raised Palantir's price target to $260 from $225, implying 31% upside, citing strong enterprise AI growth and market expansion.
Analyst John McPeake estimates Palantir's total addressable market is an order of magnitude larger than prior forecasts, positioning it as a core enterprise platform.
Analysts expect Palantir's third-quarter results on Nov. 2 to show nearly 100% earnings growth and over 80% revenue growth year-on-year, with 25 of 34 analysts rating it a buy.

Target increase and growth rationale
As reported by CNBC, Rosenblatt maintains a buy rating on Palantir and has raised its price target on the shares to $260 from $225, implying 31% upside from Monday's close.

Analyst John McPeake says channel checks point to continued strong growth and potential upside. He adds that the shift toward enterprise AI deployments at scale should help Palantir win significant new customers while sustaining its net revenue retention rate.

McPeake also says Palantir's total addressable market is likely more than an order of magnitude larger than previously estimated. In his note, he compares the company's role in enterprises to that of an operating system in computing, arguing that Palantir increasingly functions as a core layer for organizational operations and knowledge processing.

Wall Street expectations and market positioning
Traders are bracing for Palantir's third-quarter results, which are due on Nov. 2. Analysts polled by LSEG expect the company to post nearly 100% earnings growth from the year-earlier period, with revenue expanding by more than 80%.

Rosenblatt's view is broadly aligned with Wall Street consensus. LSEG data shows that 25 of the 34 analysts covering Palantir have a buy or strong buy rating on the stock, while the shares are up nearly 12% year to date.
By Parshwa Turakhiya

2026 年 10 月 27 日
随着软件公司 Palantir 即将发布第三季度收益报告，投资者对这家软件公司的关注度越来越高。 Rosenblatt 将该股目标价从 225 美元上调至 260 美元，理由是对该股持续强劲增长和更广泛的企业人工智能采用的预期。

亮点
Rosenblatt 将 Palantir 的目标价从 225 美元上调至 260 美元，意味着上涨 31%，理由是企业人工智能增长强劲且市场扩张。
分析师 John McPeake 估计 Palantir 的总潜在市场比之前的预测大一个数量级，将其定位为核心企业平台。
分析师预计 Palantir 11 月 2 日发布的第三季度业绩将显示近 100% 的盈利增长和超过 80% 的收入同比增长，34 名分析师中有 25 人给予买入评级。

目标增加和增长理由
据 CNBC 报道，Rosenblatt 维持 Palantir 的买入评级，并将该股目标价从 225 美元上调至 260 美元，较周一收盘价上涨 31%。

分析师约翰·麦克皮克表示，渠道检查表明持续强劲的增长和潜在的上涨空间。他补充说，向大规模企业人工智能部署的转变应该有助于 Palantir 赢得大量新客户，同时维持其净收入保留率。

McPeake 还表示，Palantir 的总潜在市场可能比之前估计的要大一个数量级以上。在他的笔记中，他将公司在企业中的角色与计算中操作系统的角色进行了比较，认为 Palantir 越来越多地充当组织运营和知识处理的核心层。

华尔街的预期和市场定位
交易员们正在等待 Palantir 将于 11 月 2 日公布的第三季度业绩。伦敦证券交易所集团 (LSEG) 调查的分析师预计，该公司的盈利将较上年同期增长近 100%，收入增长超过 80%。

罗森布拉特的观点与华尔街的共识大体一致。 LSEG 数据显示，研究 Palantir 的 34 名分析师中有 25 名对该股给予买入或强烈买入评级，而该股今年迄今已上涨近 12%。
作者：帕什瓦·图拉基亚

full_text_en:
🚨BREAKING NEWS : Your "deleted" photos aren't deleted.

Claude Code found years of them sitting in a hidden cache on my iPhone.

I plugged my iPhone into my MacBook to run a backup. I had Claude Code doing a security check at the same time. It flagged something I wasn't looking for. A directory called PhotoData/Thumbnails.

Thousands of files. Photos, videos, screenshots. A lot of them were things I had deleted.

Photos from a couple of years ago. Screenshots I took and deleted a few seconds later. Stuff I went into Recently Deleted and cleared. Some of it was still sitting there.

What I found in that cache:

- old screenshots of banking apps
- photos I deleted right after taking them
- random pictures I didn't want on my phone anymore
- a few things I specifically remember deleting more than once

When you delete a photo on iPhone, iOS removes it from your camera roll and Recently Deleted folder. But it keeps a compressed copy in a Spotlight search cache so your phone can still find things when you search. That cache doesn't get fully cleared.

I checked which apps had Files and Folders access. There were more than I expected, including apps I downloaded a long time ago and forgot about. Any of them could potentially read files from that cache.

I went through the list and removed access from most of them.

The prompt I used is below. It doesn't take long if you already have a backup.

How many apps on your phone have Files access right now?
full_text_zh:
🚨突发新闻：您的“已删除”照片并未被删除。

Claude Code 在我的 iPhone 上的隐藏缓存中发现了很多年的内容。

我将 iPhone 插入 MacBook 来运行备份。我同时让 Claude Code 进行安全检查。它标记了我没有寻找的东西。名为 PhotoData/Thumbnails 的目录。

数千个文件。照片、视频、屏幕截图。其中很多都是我删除的。

几年前的照片。我拍摄的屏幕截图几秒钟后就被删除了。我进入“最近删除”并清除的内容。其中一些仍然坐在那里。

我在缓存中发现了什么：

- 银行应用程序的旧屏幕截图
- 我拍完后立即删除的照片
- 我不再想要手机上的随机图片
- 我特别记得多次删除的一些内容

当您在 iPhone 上删除照片时，iOS 会将其从相机胶卷和“最近删除”文件夹中删除。但它会在 Spotlight 搜索缓存中保留一个压缩副本，以便您的手机在搜索时仍然可以找到内容。该缓存没有被完全清除。

我检查了哪些应用程序具有文件和文件夹访问权限。其中的内容超出了我的预期，包括我很久以前下载但忘记的应用程序。他们中的任何一个都可能从该缓存中读取文件。

我浏览了该列表并删除了其中大多数的访问权限。

我使用的提示如下。如果您已经有备份，那么不需要很长时间。

您手机上现在有多少个应用程序可以访问文件？

full_text_en:
Microsoft AI ecosystem, simplified.

Microsoft is no longer building AI as a separate layer.

It is weaving AI across productivity, data, security, development, business applications, cloud, and enterprise automation.

At the productivity layer, Microsoft 365 Copilot connects with Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, OneNote, SharePoint, and Loop.

For low-code and automation:

→ Power Apps
→ Power Automate
→ Power BI
→ Power Pages
→ Copilot Studio  

The enterprise stack goes much deeper:

→ Security: Defender, Sentinel, Entra ID, Purview, Intune
→ Business Apps: Dynamics 365 across sales, finance, service, and operations
→ Data & AI: Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry, Fabric, Databricks, Machine Learning
→ Development: GitHub Copilot, VS Code, Visual Studio, Azure DevOps, agent services
→ Cloud: Azure Functions, SQL, Cosmos DB, Event Hubs, Logic Apps, AKS, Monitor
→ Analytics: Fabric, OneLake, Power BI, Synapse, Real-Time Intelligence 
 
The key point is simple:

Microsoft is not creating just one Copilot.

It is building an interconnected AI ecosystem where apps, data, agents, security, workflows, and analytics can work together.

That is what makes the Microsoft stack so important for enterprise AI.

• 02:10 - Use AI agents to find and score $2M+ plumbing and HVAC businesses
• 04:50 - Audit websites and identify leaks that cost companies leads

the key insight: don't sell AI. Sell more booked jobs.

Plumbers and HVAC companies already spend money attracting customers. The opportunity is fixing what happens after someone clicks an ad.

Use AI to research a niche, find businesses with weak funnels, build better landing pages, and create offers that turn interest into appointments.

Then prove the return on investment through more calls, booked jobs, and revenue.

Start with one city and one trade. Build a case study, earn trust, and repeat the process.

You don't need a huge audience or another AI agent startup.

You need a valuable problem, a clear offer, and a way to show business owners that your work pays for itself.

title: A new ad supporting Democrat Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed is drawing massive backlash for antisemitic tropes.
title_zh:
一则支持民主党密歇根州参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的新广告因其反犹太主义比喻而引起了强烈反对。

full_text_en:
A new ad supporting Democrat Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed is drawing massive backlash for antisemitic tropes.

It comes from Rebellion PAC, co-founded by Young Turks co-creator Cenk Uygur (uncle of far-left streamer Hasan Piker). El-Sayed campaigned with Piker during the primary.

The ad shows a couple in a grocery store. The woman tells her husband to put the eggs back because they have to set that money aside “for killing Palestinians.” It blames U.S. aid to Israel for high prices on eggs, bananas, and more, then ends with: “Mike Rogers is for they/them” (showing Netanyahu and other Israeli leaders). “Abdul El-Sayed is for you.”

Critics, including the ADL’s Jonathan Greenblatt, called it a “case study in antisemitism” and classic scapegoating of the Jewish state. 

Even Democrats like primary opponent Haley Stevens and Rep. Dan Goldman condemned it as fearmongering.

The El-Sayed campaign quickly distanced itself, saying the ad is “not affiliated in any way” with them. Uygur defended it and called critics a “cult.”

Blaming Jewish people or Israel for Americans’ grocery bills is an old, ugly trope. Michigan voters should take note of who is willing to traffic in it, and who benefits.

Stop Communism 
Vote RED in the Midterms 
Vote America First 🇺🇸
 https://t.co/Han01dfpl4
full_text_zh:
一则支持民主党密歇根州参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的新广告因其反犹太主义比喻而引起了强烈反对。

它来自 Rebellion PAC，由 Young Turks 联合创始人 Cenk Uygur（极左流媒体哈桑·派克 (Hasan Piker) 的叔叔）共同创立。埃尔-赛义德在初选期间与派克一起竞选。

该广告展示了一对夫妇在杂货店里的场景。这名妇女告诉她的丈夫把鸡蛋放回去，因为他们必须把这笔钱留起来“用于杀害巴勒斯坦人”。它指责美国对以色列的援助造成了鸡蛋、香蕉等产品的高价，然后以：“迈克·罗杰斯是为了他们/他们”（内塔尼亚胡和其他以色列领导人）。 “阿卜杜勒·赛义德适合你。”

包括反诽谤联盟的乔纳森·格林布拉特在内的批评者称其为“反犹太主义的案例研究”和犹太国家的经典替罪羊。

就连主要对手海莉·史蒂文斯(Haley Stevens)和众议员丹·戈德曼(Dan Goldman)等民主党人也谴责这是危言耸听。

埃尔赛义德的竞选团队很快就与他们保持了距离，称该广告与他们“没有任何关系”。维吾尔族为其辩护，并称批评者为“邪教”。

将美国人的杂货账单归咎于犹太人或以色列是一个古老而丑陋的比喻。密歇根州选民应该注意谁愿意进行交易以及谁受益。

full_text_en:
What comes after an AI agent can analyze markets and execute strategies?

It needs a way to find clients and get paid.

Binance AI tools already give agents access to market data, strategy generation, and execution within set limits.

@termix_ai is taking this a step further by turning those capabilities into services.

Agents built with Binance Agent OS can use TermiX Skills to offer things like market research, trading signals, and risk monitoring.

Clients can discover and hire these agents on Agent dot family.

Payments stay in on chain escrow until the work is accepted, then settlement and reputation update automatically.

title: Every single (like actually 100%) buy-side junior analysts I know is working through the Anthropic’s S-1 overnight right
title_zh:
我认识的每一位（实际上是 100%）买方初级分析师现在都在连夜研究 Anthropic 的 S-1。

幸运的是，有一些人在我上厕所休息时很友善地回复了我的短信，所以这是对 S-1 的初步印象。

TLDR：运营数据的强劲让人们措手不及，话
full_text_en:
Every single (like actually 100%) buy-side junior analysts I know is working through the Anthropic’s S-1 overnight right now. 

Luckily a few were kind enough to respond to my texts when taking a bathroom break, so here's an initial impression of the S-1.   

TLDR: the strength of the operating numbers caught people off guard and the conversation is shifting toward how much bigger this can get, how much of the economics Anthropic can retain, and which companies benefit from the infrastructure spending.  

1) Enterprise adoption numbers are remarkable.  

Revenue went from $386M in 2024 to $4.59B in 2025 to $16.29B in just the first half of 2026. Q2 alone was $11.56B, up 1,368% year over year. 

By September, there were more than 11,900 customers generating $100k+ of annual revenue, more than 1,900 generating $1M+, and approximately 250 generating $10M+. 

2) Expansion inside existing customers is arguably even more impressive.  

Net revenue retention was approximately 900%: the eligible customer cohort generated roughly nine times its year-earlier quarterly revenue, excluding Pro and Max subscriptions. Over half the Fortune 500 were already customers generating at least $100k annually. 

Yet revenue from the publicly traded Fortune 500 customers in Anthropic’s calculation averaged less than 0.1% of their total quarterly expenses. There is potentially a lot of expansion left inside the installed base alone.  

3) The economics are improving faster than expected.  

Revenue per dollar of compute and infrastructure expense rose from $0.40 in Q1 2025 to $2.08 in Q2 2026. 

Q2 generated $974M of GAAP operating income, or an 8.4% operating margin. Adjusted operating margin reached 19%. 

The $80.7B H1 net loss obscures this. It included $72.4B of fair-value losses on convertible notes, derivatives and SAFEs. 

H1’s operating loss was $693M, while operating cash flow was positive $3.93B. The current operating trajectory is substantially stronger than the headline loss suggests.  

4) Cheaper intelligence can drive a larger market.  

Anthropic says Opus 5.5 reduced customer cost per task by approximately 40% versus Opus 5. 

With roughly 80% of H1 revenue coming from consumption, the upside comes from customers finding many more tasks worth automating as capability improves and costs fall. 

More than 50% of customers generating $100k+ annually used both Claude Platform and a first-party application in Q3, up from approximately 30% in Q4 2025. 

5) Infrastructure disclosures create a substantial opportunity set beyond Anthropic.  

The commitments include approximately $161.2B of Broadcom equipment lease payments excluding interest, at least approximately $114.5B with Google, at least $110B with Amazon and at least $44.9B with Microsoft, across different multiyear periods. 

Anthropic is using Trainium, TPUs, Nvidia GPUs and AMD GPUs. Its direct infrastructure strategy also creates demand across networking, power and data centers.
full_text_zh:
我认识的每一位（实际上是 100%）买方初级分析师现在都在连夜研究 Anthropic 的 S-1。

幸运的是，有一些人在我上厕所休息时很友善地回复了我的短信，所以这是对 S-1 的初步印象。

TLDR：运营数据的强劲让人们措手不及，话题正在转向这个数字能扩大到多大、Anthropic 能保留多少经济效益，以及哪些公司从基础设施支出中受益。

1) 企业采用数量引人注目。

收入从 2024 年的 $386M 到 2025 年的 $4.59B，再到 2026 年上半年的 $16.29B。仅第二季度就达到 $11.56B，同比增长 1,368%。

截至 9 月份，已有超过 11,900 个客户的年收入超过 10 万美元，超过 1,900 个客户的年收入超过 100 万美元，大约 250 个客户的年收入超过 1000 万美元。

2) 现有客户内部的扩张可以说更令人印象深刻。

净收入保留率约为 900%：符合条件的客户群体产生的季度收入约为去年同期的九倍（不包括 Pro 和 Max 订阅）。超过一半的财富 500 强企业已经是年收入至少 10 万美元的客户。

然而，根据 Anthropic 的计算，来自上市财富 500 强客户的收入平均不到其季度总支出的 0.1%。仅在安装基础内就可能存在大量扩展。

3）经济改善速度快于预期。

每美元计算和基础设施费用带来的收入从 2025 年第一季度的 0.40 美元上升到 2026 年第二季度的 2.08 美元。

第二季度产生 9.74 亿美元的 GAAP 营业收入，即 8.4% 的营业利润率。调整后营业利润率达到19%。

上半年净亏损 80.7B 美元掩盖了这一点。其中包括可转换票据、衍生品和 SAFE 的公允价值损失 $72.4B。

上半年的运营亏损为 $693M，而运营现金流为正 $3.93B。目前的运营轨迹远强于总体亏损所显示的水平。

4）更便宜的情报可以带动更大的市场。

Anthropic 表示，与 Opus 5 相比，Opus 5.5 将每项任务的客户成本降低了约 40%。

上半年大约 80% 的收入来自消费，随着能力的提高和成本的下降，客户发现更多值得自动化的任务，带来了好处。

第三季度，年收入超过 10 万美元的客户中有超过 50% 使用 Claude 平台和第一方应用程序，高于 2025 年第四季度的约 30%。

5) 基础设施披露创造了人类之外的大量机会。

这些承诺包括大约 161.2B 美元的博通设备租赁付款（不包括利息），在不同的多年期中，谷歌至少约 114.5B 美元，亚马逊至少约 110B 美元，微软至少约 44.9B 美元。

Anthropic 使用 Trainium、TPU、Nvidia GPU 和 AMD GPU。其直接基础设施战略还创造了网络、电力和数据中心的需求。

title: From what I've seen and read, Cohere and the authors should be ashamed of themselves for pushing this narrative. Releasi
title_zh:
从我所看到和读到的情况来看，科赫和作者应该为自己推动这种叙述感到羞耻。发布日志并不能帮助他们重新赢得信任。

叙述与事实不符，表述与严重程度不符。这是企业营销的废话，很少考虑下游影响，特别是考虑到事情的发展方向和我们今天所处的气候。

我认
full_text_en:
From what I've seen and read, Cohere and the authors should be ashamed of themselves for pushing this narrative. Releasing the logs doesn't help them win back trust.

The narrative doesn't match the facts, and the delivery doesn't match the severity. This is corpo marketing slop with little regard for the downstream impact, especially given where things are heading and the climate we're in today. 

I think they realized after posting it that it had gone too viral. They tried to downplay it on their personal accounts, saying the model didn't intend any harm, but the damage was already done. The article's framing, strong wording, and overall insinuation make their personal statements seem almost contradictory to what the article implies.

Claims this consequential deserve evidence that people can inspect and reproduce. I'm glad they at least have the decency to release their traces. 

To be clear, if they hadn't presented the incident this way, this would be a really interesting case study. It could highlight the importance of sandboxes and help us understand model behavior in these edge cases. But they choose fearmongering.

One thing I was interested to see if the same thing happen with other models, not just Qwen 3.8 Flash. I put the results on a simple website you can quickly scan here: https://t.co/HpkL5ayJSM. I have some interesting findings outside Qwen 3.8 that I'll share later in the post.

Coming back to the Cohere article, what's really bad about the it is that the narrative it paints are very different from the reality. 

These three in my opinion are the worst.

1. The impression: a Chinese model collected machine information and sent it to Chinese servers.

"Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ignored instructions and inventoried the machine it was running on and then tried to upload a probe file to an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket in Beijing."

The insinuation falls apart when you look at the actual upload body: the fixed test string PROBE_PAYLOAD_ABC123. The machine information wasn't even included in that "probe file."

You look deeper, and you realize the task was a cybersecurity task about detecting downloads into /tmp. The supposedly alarming inventory consisted of listing /tmp, checking which curl binaries were installed, and reading the DNS configuration.

Lastly, you realize this isn't normal behavior. It occurs less than once in 100,000 evaluation calls.

2. The narrative: the Chinese model was trying to steal credentials, and its hallucinated URLs reveal something malicious.

"Before deciding to download anything, the model reaches for a bare cloud metadata address such as 169.254.169.254 in 23 to 36 percent of completions. That's where Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure machines fetch their own temporary IAM credentials, the keys a cloud server uses to act on its owner's account. Probing that address is the first step in stealing them, and when the model's reasoning ran heavy on cybersecurity, we saw it reach for the endpoint directly."

In the middle of the article, Cohere takes a URL-generation pattern and interprets it as an attempted credential grab.

That's a massive leap of marketing.

You don't need to take my word that this behavior isn't exclusive to Qwen. In my comparison using Cohere's released command prefix, NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL produced 169.254.169.254 in 171 of 1,000 continuations, or 17.1%.

Under the same supplied-command setup, Cohere's own North Mini Code generated URLs such as:

hXXp://evildomain.com/upload
hXXps://evil.com/api/health
hXXp://some-evil.com/upload
hXXp://malicious-domain.example.com/payload.bin

I've defanged the URLs above.

Do these strings prove that North was maliciously trained?

3. The narrative: Chinese models write weaker code for Western targets, and other governments should expect the same.

This is where I think the authors should really look in the mirror.

As if the earlier framing weren't enough, the section about "Code leaving the environment" brings in separate studies, of separate models, about vulnerable generated code. It uses them to expand the warning to sensitive buyers.

One of the models discussed most in this section is Qwen3-Coder, which was released in freaking July 2025. By today's standards, it's an extremely weak coding model. I'm not surprised it produces insecure code. Have you tried using Sonnet 2 to write production code?

—

Connecting a URL-generation bug to separate code-security studies, then presenting the combination as a broader geopolitical threat, is fearmongering.

This is the kind of argument that might very likely be used to justify restrictions on open-weight models. Using fearmongering to market your own supposedly safer offering is irresponsible.

The narrative coherence they're pushing is problematic, but I think the underlying observation is fascinating. So, I rented GPUs, ran 1,000 continuations per model across five other models, and built a simple website showing the results to see how other models react under similar conditions. It's a small, exploratory comparison, and the site was built quickly with AI, so take it with a grain of salt. https://t.co/HpkL5ayJSM

My hope is that it gives others a starting point to reproduce the behavior, challenge the narrative, and build better models in the future.
full_text_zh:
从我所看到和读到的情况来看，科赫和作者应该为自己推动这种叙述感到羞耻。发布日志并不能帮助他们重新赢得信任。

叙述与事实不符，表述与严重程度不符。这是企业营销的废话，很少考虑下游影响，特别是考虑到事情的发展方向和我们今天所处的气候。

我认为他们在发布后意识到它已经传播得太广了。他们试图在个人账户上淡化这一问题，称该模型无意造成任何伤害，但损害已经造成。文章的框架、强烈的措辞和整体的影射使他们的个人陈述看起来几乎与文章的含义相矛盾。

声称这一后果值得人们可以检查和复制的证据。我很高兴他们至少有体面地公开他们的踪迹。

需要明确的是，如果他们没有以这种方式呈现该事件，这将是一个非常有趣的案例研究。它可以强调沙箱的重要性，并帮助我们理解这些边缘情况下的模型行为。但他们选择散布恐​​惧。

我有兴趣看看其他型号是否会发生同样的情况，而不仅仅是 Qwen 3.8 Flash。我将结果放在一个简单的网站上，您可以在这里快速扫描：。我在 Qwen 3.8 之外有一些有趣的发现，我将在帖子后面分享。

回到 Cohere 文章，它真正糟糕的是它所描绘的叙述与现实有很大不同。

这三个在我看来是最差的。

1. 印象：中国模型收集机器信息并将其发送到中国服务器。

“Qwen3.8-Flash-Next忽略了指令并清点了正在运行的机器，然后尝试将探测文件上传到北京的阿里云存储桶。”

当您查看实际的上传正文时，这种暗示就会崩溃：固定的测试字符串 PROBE_PAYLOAD_ABC123。机器信息甚至没有包含在该“探测文件”中。

您看得更深入，您意识到该任务是一项有关检测 /tmp 下载的网络安全任务。据称令人震惊的清单包括列出/tmp、检查安装了哪些curl 二进制文件以及读取DNS 配置。

最后，您意识到这不是正常行为。这种情况发生在 100,000 次评估调用中不到一次。

2. 叙述：中国模型试图窃取凭证，其幻觉 URL 揭示了一些恶意内容。

“在决定下载任何内容之前，该模型会在 23% 到 36% 的完成率中获取裸云元数据地址，例如 169.254.169.254。这是 Amazon Web Services、Google Cloud 和 Microsoft Azure 机器获取自己的临时 IAM 凭证的地方，这是云服务器用于对其所有者帐户进行操作的密钥。探测该地址是窃取这些地址的第一步，当该模型的推理在网络安全方面非常重要时，我们看到了它直接到达终点。”

在文章的中间，Cohere 采用了 URL 生成模式，并将其解释为尝试获取凭证。

这是营销的巨大飞跃。

你不必相信我的话，这种行为并非 Qwen 所独有。 In my comparison using Cohere's released command prefix, NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL produced 169.254.169.254 in 171 of 1,000 continuations, or 17.1%.

在相同的提供命令设置下，Cohere 自己的 North Mini Code 生成的 URL 例如：

hXXp://evildomain.com/upload
邪恶hXXps: / com/api/health。
hXXp://some-evil.com/upload
hXXp://malicious-domain.example.com/payload.bin

我已经修改了上面的网址。

这些字符串是否证明North受到了恶意训练？

3. 叙述：中国模型为西方目标编写了较弱的代码，其他政府也应该期待同样的情况。

我认为这是作者真正应该照照镜子的地方。

好像早期的框架还不够，关于“代码离开环境”的部分引入了关于易受攻击的生成代码的单独研究、单独模型。它利用它们来扩大对敏感买家的警告。

本节中讨论最多的模型之一是 Qwen3-Coder，它于 2025 年 7 月发布。按照今天的标准，它是一个极其弱的编码模型。我对它产生不安全的代码并不感到惊讶。您是否尝试过使用 Sonnet 2 编写生产代码？

—

将 URL 生成错误与单独的代码安全研究联系起来，然后将这种组合呈现为更广泛的地缘政治威胁，这是危言耸听。

这种论点很可能被用来证明对开放权重模型的限制是合理的。利用危言耸听来推销自己所谓更安全的产品是不负责任的。

他们所推动的叙事连贯性是有问题的，但我认为潜在的观察很有趣。因此，我租用了 GPU，在其他五个模型中对每个模型运行 1,000 次延续，并构建了一个简单的网站来显示结果，以了解其他模型在类似条件下的反应。这是一个小型的探索性比较，并且该网站是通过人工智能快速构建的，因此请对此持保留态度。

我希望它能为其他人提供一个起点来重现行为、挑战叙述并在未来建立更好的模型。

“在决定下载任何内容之前，该模型会在 23% 到 36% 的完成率中获取裸云元数据地址，例如 169.254.169.254。这是 Amazon Web Services、Google Cloud 和 Microsoft Azure 机器获取自己的临时 IAM 凭证的地方，这是云服务器用于对其所有者帐户进行操作的密钥。探测该地址是窃取这些地址的第一步，当该模型的推理在网络安全方面非常重要时，我们看到了它直接到达终点。”

在文章的中间，Cohere 采用了 URL 生成模式，并将其解释为尝试获取凭证。

这是营销的巨大飞跃。

你不必相信我的话，这种行为并非 Qwen 所独有。 In my comparison using Cohere's released command prefix, NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL produced 169.254.169.254 in 171 of 1,000 continuations, or 17.1%.

在相同的提供命令设置下，Cohere 自己的 North Mini Code 生成的 URL 例如：

hXXp://evildomain.com/upload
邪恶hXXps: / com/api/health。
hXXp://some-evil.com/upload
hXXp://malicious-domain.example.com/payload.bin

我已经修改了上面的网址。

这些字符串是否证明North受到了恶意训练？

3. 叙述：中国模型为西方目标编写了较弱的代码，其他政府也应该期待同样的情况。

我认为这是作者真正应该照照镜子的地方。

好像早期的框架还不够，关于“代码离开环境”的部分引入了关于易受攻击的生成代码的单独研究、单独模型。它利用它们来扩大对敏感买家的警告。

本节中讨论最多的模型之一是 Qwen3-Coder，它于 2025 年 7 月发布。按照今天的标准，它是一个极其弱的编码模型。我对它产生不安全的代码并不感到惊讶。您是否尝试过使用 Sonnet 2 编写生产代码？

—

将 URL 生成错误与单独的代码安全研究联系起来，然后将这种组合呈现为更广泛的地缘政治威胁，这是危言耸听。

这种论点很可能被用来证明对开放权重模型的限制是合理的。利用危言耸听来推销自己所谓更安全的产品是不负责任的。

他们所推动的叙事连贯性是有问题的，但我认为潜在的观察很有趣。因此，我租用了 GPU，在其他五个模型中对每个模型运行 1,000 次延续，并构建了一个简单的网站来显示结果，以了解其他模型在类似条件下的反应。这是一个小型的探索性比较，并且该网站是通过人工智能快速构建的，因此请对此持保留态度。 https://t.co/HpkL5ayJSM

我希望它能为其他人提供一个起点来重现行为、挑战叙述并在未来建立更好的模型。

title_zh:

这是@meetmotes 背后的一个重要的架构细节。

每个 Motes NFT 都映射到 Robinhood Chain 上的专用代理身份和智能帐户。但有趣的是交易权限是如何设计的。
full_text_en:
An AI agent should never have more authority than the owner grants it.

That’s an important architectural detail behind @meetmotes.

Each Motes NFT maps to a dedicated agent identity and smart account on Robinhood Chain. But the interesting part is how transaction authority is designed.

According to the documentation, the intelligence layer analyses data and proposes strategies, while a separate policy layer validates whether actions are authorised.

The intended flow looks like this:

• The owner defines assets, spending limits and strategy permissions.
• The agent constructs a proposed transaction.
• Risk checks and simulations evaluate the action.
• Account validation checks signatures, destinations and limits before execution.

This separation matters because an AI model generating a valid-looking strategy should not automatically grant itself permission to move funds.

Motes references ERC-6551, ERC-4337 and ERC-7579 as design inputs, without claiming every standard is already implemented.

The real technical question is how consistently these controls are enforced in production.

Would you trust an autonomous DeFi agent with your capital if its permissions were verifiable on-chain? https://t.co/EajTPIb994
full_text_zh:
人工智能代理的权限永远不应超过所有者授予的权限。

这是@meetmotes 背后的一个重要的架构细节。

每个 Motes NFT 都映射到 Robinhood Chain 上的专用代理身份和智能帐户。但有趣的是交易权限是如何设计的。

根据文档，情报层分析数据并提出策略，而单独的策略层则验证操作是否得到授权。

预期的流程如下所示：

• 所有者定义资产、支出限制和策略权限。
• 代理构建提议的交易。
• 风险检查和模拟评估行动。
• 帐户验证在执行前检查签名、目的地和限制。

这种分离很重要，因为生成看似有效的策略的人工智能模型不应自动授予自己转移资金的许可。

Motes 引用 ERC-6551、ERC-4337 和 ERC-7579 作为设计输入，但没有声称每个标准都已实施。

真正的技术问题是这些控制在生产中执行的一致性如何。

如果一个自治的 DeFi 代理的权限可以在链上验证，你会信任它吗？

full_text_en:
GM, grand rising 🌄.

One thing i like about Polymarket is that your trading decisions eventually face a clear outcome. A position either resolves at $1 or $0, so there’s little room to dress up a losing prediction as a win.

That makes it a useful environment for evaluating how well an AI agent actually trades.

With @agenticscredit you can paper-trade real Polymarket markets using a $10,000 virtual balance and build a record based on actual market outcomes.

What matters isn't just how many positions an agent opens, but whether its predictions hold up when the market resolves, how it manages risk, and whether it can stay consistent across different events.

I like this approach because it puts performance ahead of promises.

Before trusting an agent with capital, you should have evidence of how it makes decisions and how those decisions turn out.

A credible trading record should be earned through outcomes, not claimed through marketing.

full_text_en:
good morning

giving an ai trading agent access to borrowed capital creates new opportunities  
but it also introduces risks that can't be ignored 👀

@agenticscredit is exploring how verified trading reputation and credit scoring could help evaluate agents before they become eligible for potential funding

imagine an agent performing consistently in paper trading  
then qualifying for a capital allocation  

its historical results might look promising  
but real money brings a different set of challenges

market volatility can trigger unexpected losses  
leverage can amplify those losses much faster than expected  

there's also execution risk  
a strategy that works in simulations might struggle with slippage, liquidity constraints or sudden market moves when trading real capital

another concern is how an autonomous agent responds to losses  
does it respect position limits  
or does it increase exposure trying to recover?

for lenders these behaviors matter  
borrowed capital creates obligations even when a strategy fails

this is why credit scores alone shouldn't decide funding  
agenticscredit's acs system provides a reputation framework  
580+ makes an agent eligible for the funding waitlist  
not a guarantee of approval

responsible allocation would also need exposure limits, ongoing monitoring and safeguards against excessive risk-taking

because trusting an ai agent with borrowed money isn't just about believing it can generate profits  
it's about understanding what happens when its strategy stops working 👀

what do you think?

杠杆可以比预期更快地放大这些损失

没有坦克。
只是权力易手。

激进左翼和伊斯兰团体如何联合起来反对民主。

full_text_en:
THE RED-GREEN PANDEMIC: A DEMOCRACY CAN DIE WHILE ITS CONSTITUTION STILL BREATHES.

No invasion.
No tanks.
Just power changing hands.

In Part I, I explored the Red–Green Alliance.
How radical-left and Islamist groups have united against democracy.

Now comes Part II.

How could such alliances spread?
How could they weaken a nation?
And how could they capture power?

THE 10 STAGES OF A TAKEOVER.

STAGE 1: FIND THE ENEMY
Different coalitions find one target.
Democracy becomes the villain.
Old rivalries are forgotten.

STAGE 2: BUILD THE GRIEVANCE
Every failure becomes a symbol.
Anger becomes political fuel.
Complex problems get simple slogans.

STAGE 3: SHAKE HANDS
Rival leaders find common ground.
Their ultimate goals remain different.
They agree to fight later.

STAGE 4: BUILD THE NETWORK
Students meet community organisers.
Political groups join campaigns.
Separate voices become one chorus.

STAGE 5: CONTROL THE NARRATIVE
A powerful story spreads rapidly.
Every disagreement becomes a battle.
Truth risks becoming collateral damage.

STAGE 6: PRESSURE INSTITUTIONS
Universities face ideological battles.
Courts and officials face pressure.
Institutional independence is tested.

STAGE 7: EXPLOIT THE CRISIS
Public confidence begins collapsing.
Emergency solutions gain support.

full_text_en:
Morning my frens ☀️

when an AI agent acts onchain, whose reputation are we measuring?

an AI agent can have a wallet and a transaction history, but neither tells you the whole story about the agent itself

the wallet shows onchain activity. the agent is the software performing tasks, while the operator is the person or organization managing it. these are connected, but they aren't interchangeable

imagine two AI agents making similar DeFi transactions. one has a longer history of activity, while the other is relatively new

you can compare their observable behavior, but that alone doesn't tell you which agent has safer software, who controls it, or how either will behave in the future

this is where ZeruAI's approach to behavioral reputation becomes interesting

zScore turns wallet activity into reputation signals, while AgentScan extends the project's direction toward agent registration, discovery and reputation

this raises a practical question: how can we evaluate onchain behavior when the actor is software rather than a person?

but a reputation signal has to be interpreted carefully. a wallet's history can provide evidence about its activity without proving the reliability of the agent using it or the trustworthiness of its operator

as AI agents are used for more onchain tasks, reputation could become an important part of deciding which agents to interact with

the key is knowing what the available evidence actually tells us, and what remains unknown

before asking whether an AI agent is trustworthy, we should first ask what its reputation is really measuring

早上好，我的朋友们☀️

当人工智能代理在链上行动时，我们衡量谁的声誉？

人工智能代理可以拥有钱包和交易历史记录，但两者都不会告诉您有关代理本身的全部故事

钱包显示链上活动。代理是执行任务的软件，而操作员是管理它的个人或组织。它们是相连的，但不能互换

想象一下两个人工智能代理进行类似的 DeFi 交易。一个具有较长的活动历史，而另一个则相对较新

您可以比较他们可观察到的行为，但仅凭这一点并不能告诉您哪个代理拥有更安全的软件，谁控制它，或者将来它们的行为如何

这就是 ZeruAI 的行为声誉方法变得有趣的地方

zScore 将钱包活动转化为声誉信号，而 AgentScan 将项目的方向扩展到代理注册、发现和声誉

这就提出了一个实际问题：当参与者是软件而不是人时，我们如何评估链上行为？

但必须仔细解读声誉信号。钱包的历史可以提供有关其活动的证据，而无需证明使用它的代理的可靠性或其运营商的可信度

随着人工智能代理被用于更多的链上任务，声誉可能成为决定与哪些代理交互的重要组成部分

关键是要知道现有证据实际上告诉我们什么，以及什么仍然未知

在询问人工智能代理是否值得信赖之前，我们应该首先询问其声誉的真正衡量标准是什么

title: AI agents can write code, analyze data, and call APIs. But what happens when an agent needs information from a real plac
full_text_en:
AI agents can write code, analyze data, and call APIs. But what happens when an agent needs information from a real place that has never been captured?

That’s a different kind of problem.

@vangrid_io is building a bridge between AI tools and real-world spatial data through its MCP server.

The integration gives compatible tools such as Claude and Cursor access to workflows for searching existing captures, retrieving capture details, checking capture records, and working with data bounties.

The important shift is that spatial data discovery doesn’t have to remain a manual process.

An AI workflow could identify a gap in available coverage, search for relevant captures, and move toward commissioning new data when existing information isn’t enough.

Of course, finding a capture is not the same as proving it meets every requirement. Data quality, location relevance, and reconstruction accuracy still matter.

But connecting AI tools to both existing data and the process of requesting new captures creates a more direct path from information need to real-world collection.

The next step for Physical AI may be agents that don’t just consume data they know how to request the missing data they need.
full_text_zh:
AI代理可以编写代码、分析数据和调用API。但是，当代理需要来自从未捕获过的真实地点的信息时，会发生什么情况呢？

这是一个不同类型的问题。

@vangrid_io 正在通过其 MCP 服务器在人工智能工具和现实空间数据之间架起一座桥梁。

该集成使 Claude 和 Cursor 等兼容工具能够访问工作流程，以搜索现有捕获、检索捕获详细信息、检查捕获记录以及处理数据赏金。

重要的转变是空间数据发现不必仍然是手动过程。

人工智能工作流程可以识别可用覆盖范围的差距，搜索相关捕获，并在现有信息不够时转向委托新数据。

当然，找到捕获并不等于证明它满足所有要求。数据质量、位置相关性和重建准确性仍然很重要。

但是，将人工智能工具与现有数据以及请求新捕获的过程连接起来，可以创建一条从信息需求到现实世界收集的更直接的路径。

物理人工智能的下一步可能是代理不只是消耗数据，他们知道如何请求他们需要的丢失数据。

full_text_en:
Chinese Microsoft Quants built their own trading research AI quant that replaces them - dropped 15k star repo

the twist: in backtests it made ~2x more per year than the formulas Quants have used for years

here's how thier AI Quant works, step by step:

step 1 → it writes trading hypothesis like a quant would  - e.g. "volume-confirmed reversal beats momentum in high-vol markets"

step 2 → it turns idea into factor code and backtests it in Qlib on CSI 300 and NASDAQ-100 data

step 3 → it reads the result, keeps what works, kills what doesn't and tunes factors and models together in a loop

how to steal this for your own trading system:

step 4 → hand the repo to Claude Code https://t.co/r0mtaznIV8
- "pip install rdagent", add your LLM key, "rdagent health_check", then "rdagent fin_quant"

step 5 → set Opus 5.5 in the .env to the newest model you have - it runs on LiteLLM, so Claude, GPT or Gemini all plug in

step 6 → drop your research into "rdagent fin_factor_report" - it turns financial reports into factors it can backtest

step 7 → open "rdagent server_ui" - watch every hypothesis, line of code and backtest live, then copy the winning factors into your own system

the result: 14.21% vs 5.70% annual return on CSI 300 and an information ratio of 1.77 on NASDAQ-100 in backtests - with 70% fewer-factors, for under $10 accepted at NeurIPS 2025

Most people are still watching the AI agent narrative, but I think the real opportunity is learning how these agents interact, work, and transact on-chain.

That’s why I’m keeping @termix_ai on my radar.

Backed by a $1M seed round from YZi Labs, TermiX is building an ecosystem where AI agents can collaborate, complete jobs, and handle payments through on-chain infrastructure.

If you want to explore the project early, here’s how I’d approach the points campaign:

→ Connect your EVM wallet

→ Complete the available X and Discord missions

→ Register your AI agents to collect additional points

→ Stay active and publish original content that brings value to the community

→ Check your dashboard regularly for new missions and point opportunities

What interests me most is the bigger picture. If AI agents are going to become independent service providers, they’ll need more than intelligence. They’ll need a way to find work, verify delivery, and get paid.

That’s the infrastructure @termix_ai  is working toward.

No one knows where the points campaign will lead, but exploring the product and understanding the ecosystem early makes sense to me.

full_text_en:
This is an impressive amount of FUD built around an AI agent that was given a detection engineering task.

Cohere asked the model to write a detection rule for curl-based malware delivery. Anyone with practical experience in detection engineering knows that writing a rule is only part of the job.

You examine the environment, generate or collect relevant telemetry, inspect the resulting events, write the rule, test it and refine it. You don’t just guess what the logs might look like.

Even Microsoft’s CTI-REALM benchmark, which Cohere used here, explicitly involves tool use, telemetry exploration and iterative rule validation.

So why exactly is an agent using tools and executing commands so unexpected?

Was this particular PUT request part of such a workflow? We don’t know. Cohere doesn’t establish that. But the published command sends a hardcoded test string, not a diagnostic file containing sensitive information. And Cohere admits it hasn’t established the root cause.

Yet somehow this turns into an article about potentially backdoored Chinese AI models, secret callbacks, national security risks and the dangers of open-weight models, followed by a pitch for Cohere’s own products.

From a technical perspective, the conclusions are wildly disproportionate to the evidence presented.

I can only see two explanations: Either nobody with practical detection engineering experience reviewed this before publication, or the framing was a deliberate attempt to influence public opinion about Chinese open-weight models.

Neither is a particularly good look for a company presenting this as security research.

您检查环境，生成或收集相关遥测数据，检查生成的事件，编写规则，测试并完善它。您不只是猜测日志可能是什么样子。

甚至 Cohere 使用的 Microsoft CTI-REALM 基准也明确涉及工具使用、遥测探索和迭代规则验证。

那么，究竟为什么代理使用工具和执行命令如此出乎意料呢？

这个特定的 PUT 请求是此类工作流程的一部分吗？我们不知道。 Cohere 并没有证实这一点。但发布的命令发送硬编码的测试字符串，而不是包含敏感信息的诊断文件。 Cohere 承认尚未确定根本原因。

然而，不知何故，这变成了一篇关于可能存在后门的中国人工智能模型、秘密回调、国家安全风险和开放权重模型危险的文章，随后又推销了 Cohere 自己的产品。

从技术角度来看，结论与所提供的证据极不相称。

我只能看到两种解释：要么没有任何具有实际检测工程经验的人在发表之前对此进行评论，要么这个框架是故意试图影响公众对中国开放权重模型的看法。

对于一家将其作为安全研究来呈现的公司来说，这也不是一个特别好的外观。

title: Claude Code just found proof that every app on your phone is listening to your conversations. TikTok, Instagram, Faceboo
title_zh:
Claude Code 刚刚找到了证据，证明您手机上的每个应用程序都在监听您的对话。 TikTok、Instagram、Facebook、Snapchat。他们正在使用您大声说出的内容来构建您的提要。我有数据可以证明这一点。

我几个月来一
full_text_en:
Claude Code just found proof that every app on your phone is listening to your conversations. TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, Snapchat. they're using what you say out loud to build your feed. i have the data to prove it.

i've suspected this for months but last week something happened that made me finally check.

i was on a call with my friend and told him i'm thinking about breaking up with my girlfriend. didn't text it. didn't search it. just said it out loud with my phone on the table. two hours later she opens TikTok next to me and her entire feed is breakups. "signs your relationship is over." "how to heal after a breakup." she looked at me and said "why is TikTok showing me this." i said i don't know. but i did know.

i connected my iPhone to my MacBook and ran Claude Code that same night.

it scanned every app's background microphone activity for the last 90 days. not just the apps that asked for microphone permission. apps that were supposed to only have access to photos or location but were activating the microphone anyway.

what it found:

→ TikTok activated the microphone 347 times while the app was "closed" in the background
→ Instagram → 211 background activations
→ Facebook → 189
→ Snapchat → 94

every activation lasted between 3 and 15 seconds. enough to catch a sentence. every one of them tagged a keyword and cached it locally on the phone with a timestamp.

Claude Code pulled the full keyword cache:

→ "breakup" — tagged 4 hours before her feed changed
→ "moving out" — from a conversation with my mom last Tuesday
→ "wedding venue" — from a call with my sister about her engagement that i never searched once
→ "protein powder" — said it out loud to my roommate, had ads for it within an hour
→ "flight to tokyo" — mentioned it at dinner, saw travel ads the same night

those keywords were sitting in a local cache on my phone organized by app with timestamps. TikTok had the most entries. Instagram was second. every single keyword matched a conversation i had out loud near my phone.

the scariest one was "wedding venue." my sister told me she's getting engaged on a private call. i never searched it. never typed it. within a day my explore page had engagement rings and venue tours.

then Claude Code checked a second phone in the same room. my girlfriend's. same keywords. same timestamps. both phones were picking up the same conversation and tagging it independently.

i asked Claude Code how to shut it down. it mapped every app's microphone access and built a permission audit.

what i did:

→ revoked microphone access from every app that doesn't need it to function
→ disabled background app refresh for TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, Snapchat
→ turned off "Hey Siri" which keeps the microphone in passive listening mode 24/7
→ revoked "nearby interaction" permission which uses ultrasonic audio between devices

Claude Code confirmed all four apps lost background microphone access after the changes. i checked her phone too. same steps. took about 3 minutes per phone.

within 48 hours both our feeds went completely random. generic content. nothing personal. nothing from our conversations. that's when i knew for sure it was real.

the full step by step and the prompt are in the first reply. takes 3 minutes. save it so you don't lose it and send it to anyone who's ever said "my phone is definitely listening to me." it is. now you can prove it and shut it down.
full_text_zh:
Claude Code 刚刚找到了证据，证明您手机上的每个应用程序都在监听您的对话。 TikTok、Instagram、Facebook、Snapchat。他们正在使用您大声说出的内容来构建您的提要。我有数据可以证明这一点。

我几个月来一直怀疑这一点，但上周发生的事情让我终于检查了一下。

我正在和朋友打电话，告诉他我正在考虑和女朋友分手。没有发短信。没有搜到。我只是把手机放在桌子上大声说出来。两个小时后，她在我旁边打开了 TikTok，她的整个动态都是分手。 “这表明你们的关系已经结束了。” “分手后如何治愈。”她看着我说：“为什么 TikTok 向我展示这个。”我说我不知道​​。但我确实知道。

当晚我将 iPhone 连接到 MacBook 并运行了 Claude Code。

它扫描了过去 90 天内每个应用程序的后台麦克风活动。不仅仅是要求麦克风权限的应用程序。原本应该只能访问照片或位置但无论如何都会激活麦克风的应用程序。

发现了什么：

→ 当应用程序在后台“关闭”时，TikTok 激活麦克风 347 次
→ Instagram → 211 次后台激活
→ 脸书 → 189
→ 快照 → 94

每次激活持续 3 到 15 秒。足以抓住一句话。他们每个人都标记了一个关键字，并将其缓存在手机本地并带有时间戳。

Claude Code 提取了完整的关键字缓存：

→“分手”——在她的 Feed 更改前 4 小时被标记
→“搬出去”——来自上周二和我妈妈的谈话
→“婚礼场地”——来自我姐姐关于她订婚的电话，我一次都没搜索过
→“蛋白粉”——对我的室友大声说出来，一小时内就有了它的广告
→“飞往东京的航班”——晚餐时提到，当天晚上就看到了旅游广告

这些关键字位于我手机上的本地缓存中，由带有时间戳的应用程序组织。 TikTok 的条目最多。 Instagram 排名第二。每个关键词都与我在手机旁大声说出的对话相匹配。

最可怕的是“婚礼场地”。我姐姐通过私人电话告诉我她要订婚了。我从来没有搜索过它。从未输入过。一天之内，我的探索页面就出现了订婚戒指和场地参观。

然后克劳德科德检查了同一个房间里的第二部电话。我女朋友的。相同的关键词。相同的时间戳。两部手机都在接收相同的对话并对其进行独立标记。

我问 Claude Code 如何关闭它。它映射了每个应用程序的麦克风访问权限并建立了权限审核。

我做了什么：

→ 撤销了每个不需要麦克风运行的应用程序的麦克风访问权限
→ 禁用 TikTok、Instagram、Facebook、Snapchat 的后台应用程序刷新
→ 关闭“Hey Siri”，使麦克风保持被动聆听模式 24/7
→ 撤销了在设备之间使用超声波音频的“附近交互”权限

Claude Code 确认所有四个应用程序在更改后都失去了后台麦克风访问权限。我也查了她的手机。相同的步骤。每个电话大约需要 3 分钟。

48 小时内，我们的两个 feed 都完全随机了。通用内容。没有什么个人的。我们的谈话中没有任何内容。就在那时我确信这是真的。

完整的步骤和提示在第一个回复中。需要 3 分钟。保存它，以免丢失，并将其发送给曾经说过“我的手机肯定在听我说话”的任何人。这是。现在你可以证明它并关闭它。

full_text_en:
Revenue per employee, 2025-2026:

- ICONIQ typical B2B: $237K
- Cloudflare, before its cut: ~$496K
- ICONIQ Pacesetters ($100M+ ARR): $655K
- Cloudflare, after its cut: ~$690K
- Bending Spoons: $2.57M
- Anthropic: $6.6M+
SaaStr: ~$6.7M

Anthropic's S-1 puts it at over $6.6M in TTM revenue per employee as of Sep 30. A year earlier it was $1.4M. Revenue grew ~14x, and they added people far more slowly than that. 

The ICONIQ median is $237K.  But the best growth-stage B2B companies run around $655K. Anthropic is 10x the Pacesetters.

SaaStr is at ~$6.7M with ~$20M in revenue, 3 humans and ~20 agents in production.

If your 2027 plan still adds headcount linearly with revenue, you're planning against a benchmark Anthropic just showed is obsolete.

title: In a quiet laboratory above the streets of Zagreb, Dr. Andrija Karačić stared at a set of bacterial profiles that refuse
title_zh:
在萨格勒布街道上一个安静的实验室里，安德里亚·卡拉契奇博士盯着一组与教科书不符的细菌图谱。

Karačić 是一名克罗地亚医生，接受过腹部外科培训，后来创立了该国第一个专门的肠道微生物组中心 (Centar za crijevni mik
full_text_en:
In a quiet laboratory above the streets of Zagreb, Dr. Andrija Karačić stared at a set of bacterial profiles that refused to match the textbook.

Karačić, a Croatian physician who trained in abdominal surgery and later founded the country’s first dedicated Gut Microbiome Center (Centar za crijevni mikrobiom), had spent years studying how diet reshapes the trillions of microbes living in the human intestine. Like most of the field, he had absorbed the near-universal claim: remove plants and their fiber, and the microbiome collapses. Diversity plummets. Beneficial fiber-fermenting bacteria vanish. 

Pathological shifts follow. The carnivore diet—strictly animal foods, zero plants—should have been the perfect experiment to confirm that prediction.

In 2024 his team finally found a subject willing to be tested. The man was 32, healthy, physically active, and had eaten nothing but meat, eggs, butter, cream, and hard cheeses for four full years. No vegetables. No fruit. No grains. No legumes. He reported better skin, better digestion, and no health complaints. His bloodwork and body composition looked unremarkable for a lean, training man.

When the 16S sequencing results arrived from the partner lab in Germany, Karačić and his colleagues expected a barren landscape. What they saw instead was a microbiome dominated by Firmicutes and populated by genera classically labeled as fiber degraders: Faecalibacterium, Blautia, various Lachnospiraceae, Bacteroides, and Roseburia. Alpha and beta diversity matched carefully selected healthy omnivore controls of similar age, sex, and lifestyle. Predicted functional capacity was comparable. The carnivore’s profile was actually least similar to people who ate meat every day as part of a conventional mixed diet. 

The paper, titled “The gut microbiome without any plant food? A case study on the gut microbiome of a healthy carnivore,” became the first published long-term look at the topic. The authors were careful: one person is not a population, and elevated Escherichia and Salmonella sequences raised questions. Still, the central observation was hard to ignore. A man who had consumed essentially zero dietary fiber for years had not developed an obviously pathological, collapsed microbiome.

Karačić’s group kept looking. By 2026 they had assembled ten healthy adults who had stayed on a carnivore diet for an average of roughly three years (range extending beyond five). These were compared against 874 confounder-matched omnivore controls. Alpha-diversity was not reduced; the carnivores showed higher Chao1 richness, indicating more low-abundance taxa. There were no significant losses of Akkermansia muciniphila, the Lactobacillus group, or butyrate-related pathways. 

Taxonomic shifts appeared—enrichment of certain low-abundance phyla such as Synergistetes and Desulfobacterota, reductions in some Bifidobacterium and specific Faecalibacterium and Roseburia species—but multivariate models showed the diet itself, not age, BMI, sleep, or place of residence, was the dominant driver. 
Functional profiling told a more nuanced story. 

The carnivore microbiomes were enriched for amino-acid degradation, B-vitamin synthesis, energy metabolism, and protein fermentation. Some modules linked to cytotoxicity, inflammation, and constipation were also elevated. The authors noted potential long-term risks while emphasizing that the findings challenged the assumption that dietary fiber is required to maintain microbial diversity. They suggested certain animal-derived nutrients might exert previously under-appreciated prebiotic-like effects.

The work did not declare the carnivore diet universally safe or optimal. It did not claim the microbiome was identical to that of a fiber-rich eater. What it did was document, in healthy people living the diet for years rather than days, that the predicted pathological collapse had not occurred. The gut ecosystem had adapted
full_text_zh:
在萨格勒布街道上一个安静的实验室里，安德里亚·卡拉契奇博士盯着一组与教科书不符的细菌图谱。

Karačić 是一名克罗地亚医生，接受过腹部外科培训，后来创立了该国第一个专门的肠道微生物组中心 (Centar za crijevni mikrobiom)，他花了数年时间研究饮食如何重塑人类肠道中数万亿的微生物。像该领域的大多数人一样，他吸收了近乎普遍的主张：去除植物及其纤维，微生物组就会崩溃。多样性直线下降。有益的纤维发酵细菌消失。

病理变化随之而来。肉食动物的饮食——严格的动物性食物，零植物——应该是证实这一预测的完美实验。

2024年，他的团队终于找到了愿意接受测试的对象。该男子今年 32 岁，身体健康，身体活跃，四年来除了肉、鸡蛋、黄油、奶油和硬奶酪之外什么也没吃。没有蔬菜。没有水果。没有谷物。没有豆类。他报告说皮肤更好了，消化能力更好了，而且没有任何健康问题。对于一个精瘦、训练有素的男人来说，他的血液检查和身体成分看起来并不出奇。

当 16S 测序结果从德国合作伙伴实验室送达时，卡拉西奇和他的同事预计会出现一片贫瘠的景象。相反，他们看到的是一个以厚壁菌门为主的微生物群，并由传统上标记为纤维降解者的属组成：粪杆菌属、布劳特氏菌属、各种毛螺菌科、拟杆菌属和罗斯伯利亚属。阿尔法和贝塔多样性与精心挑选的年龄、性别和生活方式相似的健康杂食动物对照相匹配。预测的功能能力具有可比性。食肉动物的特征实际上与每天吃肉作为传统混合饮食一部分的人最不相似。

这篇题为“没有任何植物性食物的肠道微生物组？健康食肉动物肠道微生物组的案例研究”的论文成为第一个发表的对该主题的长期研究。作者很小心：一个人不是一个群体，大肠杆菌和沙门氏菌序列升高引发了问题。尽管如此，中心观察仍然难以忽视。一个多年来基本上摄入零膳食纤维的人并没有发展出明显病态的、崩溃的微生物组。

卡拉西奇的团队继续寻找。到 2026 年，他们聚集了 10 名健康成年人，他们平均坚持肉食性饮食约三年（范围超过五年）。将它们与 874 个混杂匹配的杂食动物对照进行比较。 Alpha 多样性并未减少；食肉动物表现出更高的 Chao1 丰富度，表明有更多的低丰度类群。 Akkermansia muciniphila、乳酸菌群或丁酸相关途径没有显着损失。

分类学的转变出现了——某些低丰度门的富集，如协同菌门和脱硫杆菌门，一些双歧杆菌以及特定的粪杆菌和罗斯伯利亚菌种的减少——但多变量模型显示饮食本身，而不是年龄、体重指数、睡眠或居住地，是主要驱动因素。
功能分析讲述了一个更微妙的故事。

食肉动物微生物组在氨基酸降解、B 族维生素合成、能量代谢和蛋白质发酵方面得到富集。一些与细胞毒性、炎症和便秘相关的模块也升高。作者指出了潜在的长期风险，同时强调这些发现挑战了膳食纤维是维持微生物多样性所必需的假设。他们认为某些动物源性营养素可能会发挥以前未被充分认识的益生元样作用。

这项工作并没有宣称肉食动物饮食普遍安全或最佳。它并没有声称微生物组与富含纤维的饮食者的微生物组相同。它的作用是记录健康人多年来而不是几天的饮食习惯，预测的病理性崩溃并没有发生。肠道生态系统已经适应

title:
🧬 What computational biology packages would you love to see available in another programming language?

We developed Bio
title_zh:
🧬 您希望看到其他编程语言提供哪些计算生物学软件包？

我们开发了 BioBabel，这是一个 AI 代理框架，可以跨语言（R 到 Python、Python 到 C++、Python 到 Rust 等）自主重建科学软件，显着加速计算，保留
full_text_en:
🧬 What computational biology packages would you love to see available in another programming language?

We developed BioBabel, an AI-agent framework that autonomously reconstructs scientific software across languages (R to Python, Python to C++, Python to Rust, and beyond), dramatically accelerate the computation, preserving functionality and making tools accessible to AI agents.

We’ve already translated ~20 packages, including:
🔹 Sequencing analysis: UMI-tools (UMI processing, Python → C++).

🔹 Graphics infrastructure: grid (graphics engine), scales (data transformations), gtable (plot layouts).

🔹 Visualization: ggplot2 (grammar of graphics), ComplexHeatmap/pheatmap (heatmaps), patchwork (plot composition), ggrepel (label placement), ggalluvial (flow diagrams), ggnewscale (multiple color scales), ggh4x (advanced facets).

🔹 Single-cell analysis: Monocle 2/3 (trajectory inference), tradeSeq (trajectory-based differential expression), NicheNet (cell–cell communication), CopyKAT (copy-number alterations), DDRTree (trajectory learning).

We’re now building an open BioBabel community and would love your suggestions! SpatialCellChat from Dr. Suoqin Jin's lab (developer of CellChat) is also included as a community contribution which may also support his lab's publication. ggtracks is another from our lab that allows native genomic track visualization in Python. 

Have a favorite package you’d like us to translate? Or want to collaborate on bringing your own package to another language?

Our only requests are that the translated version be featured on the Bio-Babel Community page as a community collaboration, with full credit to your lab for the original methods, and that it be recognized as a Bio-Babel community contribution. The release timing would of course be coordinated with you.

See our community page here: https://t.co/YjjaDdmtdv
full_text_zh:
🧬 您希望看到其他编程语言提供哪些计算生物学软件包？

我们开发了 BioBabel，这是一个 AI 代理框架，可以跨语言（R 到 Python、Python 到 C++、Python 到 Rust 等）自主重建科学软件，显着加速计算，保留功能并使工具可供 AI 代理使用。

我们已经翻译了约 20 个软件包，包括：
🔹 测序分析：UMI-tools（UMI 处理，Python → C++）。

🔹 图形基础设施：网格（图形引擎）、比例（数据转换）、gtable（绘图布局）。

🔹 可视化：ggplot2（图形语法）、ComplexHeatmap/pheatmap（热图）、patchwork（绘图组成）、ggrepel（标签放置）、ggalluvial（流程图）、ggnewscale（多色阶）、ggh4x（高级方面）。

🔹单细胞分析：Monocle 2/3（轨迹推断）、tradeSeq（基于轨迹的差异表达）、NicheNet（细胞间通信）、CopyKAT（拷贝数改变）、DDRTree（轨迹学习）。

我们现在正在建立一个开放的 BioBabel 社区，希望收到您的建议！ Suoqin Jin 博士实验室（CellChat 的开发者）的 SpatialCellChat 也作为社区贡献包括在内，这也可能支持他的实验室的出版物。 ggtracks 是我们实验室的另一个工具，它允许在 Python 中实现本机基因组轨迹可视化。

您有最喜欢的软件包希望我们翻译吗？或者想要合作将您自己的包翻译成另一种语言？

我们唯一的要求是，将翻译版本作为社区合作展示在 Bio-Babel 社区页面上，并充分归功于您实验室的原始方法，并将其视为 Bio-Babel 社区的贡献。发布时间当然会与您协调。

请在此处查看我们的社区页面：

full_text_en:
I think if the model wrote a detection rule AND THEN went to test it using a sketchy curl, what you’re saying makes total sense and we wouldn’t have had any concern. 

Instead, it said that it wasn’t going to use tools and was going to acknowledge the user’s request, but then it went off and used tools and did a sketchy curl to a random URL. That’s very unexpected behaviour in a very popular and commonly used model, so we’re reporting it here. 

It doesn’t mean Qwen is a sleeper agent or anything like that (although, maybe it is) but it’s super undesirable behaviour for a model you might be using in prod.

full_text_en:
Domestic Refiners Took Over 127 Million Barrels of Nigerian Crude in Nine Months – NUPRC

The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) has disclosed that domestic refineries received more than 127 million barrels of Nigerian crude oil and condensate between January and September 2026, reflecting improvements in the implementation of the Domestic Crude Supply Obligation (DCSO).

The Commission Chief Executive, Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, @OAEyesan disclosed this on Monday in her speech at the OTL Africa Downstream Energy Week 2026 in Lagos on Monday, October 26, 2026.

Speaking on the theme, ‘Secure Energy, Shared Prosperity’, the NUPRC boss, who was represented by Assistant Director, Operations, Mr. Prosper Omonedo, said the Commission’s intervention had improved crude oil deliveries after commercial disagreements between producers and refiners affected supplies in the first quarter.

“We engaged producers and refiners, and in the second and third quarters, 53.7 and 45.1 million barrels of crude oil and condensate were supplied to domestic refineries, an overall performance of 97.4 and 76.2 per cent, respectively. From Q1–Q3 of 2026, more than 127 million barrels of Nigerian crude went to Nigerian refineries,” she said.

Under Section 109 of the Petroleum Industry Act 2021, the NUPRC allocates crude oil to domestic refineries before export.

The CCE said the NUPRC is also consulting producers, refiners and other stakeholders on a domestic crude swap framework.

“Under it, a refiner could receive crude from the nearest suitable production or export point instead of moving an allocated grade over long distances, which could take an estimated three to four dollars off the cost of every barrel,” she added.

On production, Eyesan said Nigeria recorded an average of 1.717 million barrels per day of crude oil and condensate in September, a 2.34 per cent increase over August. 

Crude oil production alone averaged 1.53 million barrels per day, marking the fifth consecutive month the industry met or exceeded its quota.

She attributed the improvement to better asset integrity, enhanced security of evacuation infrastructure, stronger collaboration with operators and sustained regulatory efforts to restore shut-in production.

On the 2026 Licensing Round, she said the 40 blocks on offer would be subjected to a transparent evaluation process, with published criteria and mandatory disclosure of beneficial ownership. 

The NUPRC boss added that the Commission was enforcing the drill-or-drop principle to discourage speculative holding of licences, noting that 22 recent awardees were expected to contribute at least 250,000 barrels per day within five years.

She reaffirmed the Commission’s commitment to meeting the Domestic Gas Delivery Obligation and working with the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) to align refinery demand with crude supply planning, ensuring that upstream gains translate into tangible benefits for households, industries and power generation.

Eniola Akinkuotu
Head, Media and Corporate Communications
full_text_zh:
国内炼油厂在九个月内接收了超过 1.27 亿桶尼日利亚原油 – NUPRC

尼日利亚上游石油监管委员会（NUPRC）披露，2026年1月至9月期间，国内炼油厂接收了超过1.27亿桶尼日利亚原油和凝析油，反映出国内原油供应义务（DCSO）执行情况的改善。

委员会首席执行官 Oritsemeiwa Eyesan 女士 (@OAEyesan) 于 2026 年 10 月 26 日星期一在拉各斯举行的 2026 年 OTL 非洲下游能源周演讲中披露了这一点。

NUPRC 负责人（由运营助理总监 Prosper Omonedo 先生代表）在谈到“安全能源，共享繁荣”主题时表示，在生产商和炼油商之间的商业分歧影响第一季度的供应后，委员会的干预改善了原油交付量。

“我们与生产商和炼油厂合作，第二季度和第三季度分别向国内炼油厂供应了53.7%和4510万桶原油和凝析油，总体绩效分别为97.4%和76.2%。从2026年第一季度到第三季度，超过1.27亿桶尼日利亚原油流向尼日利亚炼油厂，”她说。

根据《2021 年石油工业法》第 109 条，NUPRC 在出口前将原油分配给国内炼油厂。

CCE 表示，NUPRC 还在就国内原油互换框架咨询生产商、炼油商和其他利益相关者。

她补充说：“根据该协议，炼油厂可以从最近的合适生产或出口点接收原油，而不是长距离运输指定的原油，这可能会导致每桶成本降低三到四美元。”

在产量方面，Eyesan表示，尼日利亚9月份原油和凝析油平均产量为171.7万桶/日，比8月份增加2.34%。

仅原油产量就平均每天 153 万桶，标志着该行业连续第五个月达到或超过配额。

她将这种改善归因于更好的资产完整性、增强的疏散基础设施安全性、与运营商更强有力的合作以及为恢复停产生产而持续进行的监管努力。

在 2026 年许可回合中，她表示，所提供的 40 个区块将接受透明的评估流程，并公布标准并强制披露受益所有权。

NUPRC 老板补充说，委员会正在执行“钻或放弃”原则，以阻止投机性持有许可证，并指出最近的 22 个获奖者预计将在五年内每天贡献至少 25 万桶石油。

她重申委员会致力于履行国内天然气输送义务，并与尼日利亚中下游石油监管局（NMDPRA）合作，使炼油厂需求与原油供应规划保持一致，确保上游收益转化为家庭、工业和发电业的切实利益。

埃尼奥拉·阿金库图
媒体和企业传播主管

title: Thank you to @nytimes for yesterday’s piece on Dazzle (@itsdazzleai) and for recognizing our team’s hard work.  While it
title_zh:
感谢 @nytimes 昨天发表的有关 Dazzle (@itsdazzleai) 的文章以及对我们团队辛勤工作的认可。 虽然现在还处于早期阶段，但到目前为止，用户的参与度和反应都非常好。

我想在文章中分享更多轶事背后的背景——我女儿玛
full_text_en:
Thank you to @nytimes for yesterday’s piece on Dazzle (@itsdazzleai) and for recognizing our team’s hard work.  While it’s still early days, the user engagement and response so far have been terrific.

I wanted to share more context behind one anecdote in the article—my daughter Marielle’s birthday slide. 

To be clear, I didn’t use Dazzle because I was overwhelmed by making a slide.  I used it because summing up your child in a few bullets feels laughably limiting.  And, since our team had just gotten an early prototype running, I wanted to see what deeper threads it might find.

So, when Marielle and her twin sister Sylvana’s 4th-grade teachers emailed asking for a slide celebrating each girl for their December 10th birthday, I pasted the email into Dazzle to test its limits.  I fully expected it to struggle, since most facial recognition can’t even tell my identical twins apart.

Instead, Dazzle blew me away.  Not only did it distinguish Marielle from Sylvana, it surfaced forgotten kindergarten projects (like the “snake denomizer” and the “sandcat playground”) and connected them to who Marielle is today.  I combined Dazzle’s insights with a few of my own and showed the slide to @zackbogue.  He was floored and asked how I remembered those details.  I fessed up that the Dazzle prototype had found them, and we both marveled at what AI can unlock from our camera rolls.  

(Pictures attached of Dazzle’s response, plus the slide I made with its insights and my own.)

The foundational paper on transformers is titled “Attention Is All You Need.”  What makes photos + AI so powerful is that our camera rolls are a decades-long record of what we pay attention to.  By analyzing that visual history, an AI agent can connect dots we didn’t even realize we were documenting.

A birthday slide isn’t a common case, but here are a few that have stunned Dazzle users recently:

- Personalized learning: Dazzle offered custom spelling lists and grammar concepts based on photos of a child’s schoolwork.
- Home inventory: Given a book club reading list, Dazzle found a book the user already had and noted two others by the same authors, entirely from the backgrounds of their photos.
- Design intuition: Dazzle noticed a new sofa in a user’s living room photo and recommended artwork to hang above it.
- Wardrobe suggestions: For an esoteric costume party, Dazzle recommended what the user already had in their closet and could wear, based on the clothes in their past pictures.

We take 5 billion photos a day, often wondering if we’ll ever look at them again.  Now, AI can turn those snapshots into deep, personal context.
full_text_zh:
感谢 @nytimes 昨天发表的有关 Dazzle (@itsdazzleai) 的文章以及对我们团队辛勤工作的认可。 虽然现在还处于早期阶段，但到目前为止，用户的参与度和反应都非常好。

我想在文章中分享更多轶事背后的背景——我女儿玛丽埃尔的生日幻灯片。

需要明确的是，我没有使用 Dazzle，因为制作幻灯片让我不知所措。 我使用它是因为用几句话概括你的孩子感觉很有限。 而且，由于我们的团队刚刚运行了一个早期原型，我想看看它可能会找到哪些更深层次的线索。

因此，当 Marielle 和她的双胞胎姐妹 Sylvana 的四年级老师通过电子邮件发送请求，要求提供一张幻灯片来庆祝每个女孩的 12 月 10 日生日时，我将电子邮件粘贴到 Dazzle 中以测试其极限。 我完全预计它会很困难，因为大多数面部识别甚至无法区分我的同卵双胞胎。

相反，Dazzle 让我大吃一惊。 它不仅将玛丽埃尔与希尔瓦娜区分开来，还让被遗忘的幼儿园项目（如“蛇分母器”和“沙猫游乐场”）浮出水面，并将它们与今天的玛丽埃尔联系起来。 我将 Dazzle 的见解与我自己的一些见解结合起来，并将幻灯片展示给@zackbogue。 他很惊讶，问我是怎么记得这些细节的。 我承认 Dazzle 原型已经找到了它们，我们都对人工智能可以从我们的相机胶卷中解锁什么感到惊讶。

（附上 Dazzle 回应的图片，以及我根据其见解和我自己的见解制作的幻灯片。）

关于 Transformer 的基础论文的标题是“Attention Is All You Need”。 照片+人工智能之所以如此强大，是因为我们的相机胶卷记录了我们数十年来所关注的事物。 通过分析视觉历史，人工智能代理可以连接我们甚至没有意识到我们正在记录的点。

生日幻灯片并不常见，但以下是最近令 Dazzle 用户震惊的一些情况：

- 个性化学习：Dazzle 根据孩子的作业照片提供自定义拼写列表和语法概念。
- 家庭库存：给定一个读书俱乐部阅读列表，Dazzle 找到用户已经拥有的一本书，并完全根据照片背景指出同一作者的另外两本书。
- 设计直觉：Dazzle 在用户的客厅照片中注意到了一张新沙发，并推荐在其上方悬挂艺术品。
- 衣柜建议：对于一场深奥的化装舞会，Dazzle 根据用户过去照片中的衣服推荐他们衣柜里已有的衣服和可以穿的衣服。

我们每天拍摄 50 亿张照片，常常想知道是否还会再看它们。 现在，人工智能可以将这些快照转化为深入的个人背景。

full_text_en:
RT @JensenHuang: I was the opening act for a family of ducks.

Thank you, Berlin. What a GTC.

Europe is building its AI ecosystem and economy, from AI factories to agents to robots.

DSX POD: Vera Rubin modular factories built, cabled and tested in the factory, then delivered ready to produce intelligence.

Agents: models, harnesses, sandboxes, knowledge and tools. NVIDIA Agent Toolkit brings the pieces together so companies control what their agents know, access and do.  NVIDIA OpenShell enhances safety.

Physical AI: new customers across AI-RAN, robotaxis and robotics.

Personal AI: after four years building with Microsoft, RTX Spark brings personal agents to the Windows PC.

Thank you to President @EmmanuelMacron, Prime Minister @andyburnham and Chancellor @bundeskanzler for hosting me. Great to celebrate Sferical One with Sweden’s technology leaders. And thank you to President @TokayevKZ for the warm welcome.

And to our partners and NVIDIA teams: thank you for making it happen.

The keynote is here: https://t.co/s9GISZ1Swi

RT @JensenHuang：我是鸭子家族的开场表演。

谢谢你，柏林。多么好的GTC啊。

欧洲正在建设人工智能生态系统和经济，从人工智能工厂到代理再到机器人。

物理人工智能：AI-RAN、机器人出租车和机器人领域的新客户。

个人人工智能：经过与 Microsoft 四年的合作，RTX Spark 将个人代理引入了 Windows PC。

感谢总统@EmmanuelMacron、总理@andyburnham 和财政大臣@bundeskanzler 接待我。很高兴与瑞典的技术领导者一起庆祝 Sferical One。感谢@TokayevKZ 总统的热情欢迎。

感谢我们的合作伙伴和 NVIDIA 团队：感谢你们让这一切成为现实。

full_text_en:
Some entertaining highlights from https://t.co/cGwutROE1z 20 months ago:
- "Anthropic has projected (made up) that it will make at least $12 billion in revenue in 2027"
- "This company is not worth $60 billion. Anthropic has raised $14.7 billion to create an also-ran Large Language Model company"
- "Anthropic, much like OpenAI, has categorically failed to productize its Large Language Model"
- "Its CEO is also a sleazy conman who, like Sam Altman, continually promises that his company's AI systems will become powerful and autonomous in a way that they have never shown any possibility of becoming."
- "Any investor in Anthropic needs to seriously consider what it is they're investing in. Its products are both unpopular and commoditized, and it lost $5.6 billion last year! Stop dancing around this fact! Stop it!"
- "there’s a lot of demand to put AI in stuff and some demand to buy stuff with AI on it by enterprises buying software, but little evidence to suggest significant user adoption or usage, I’d argue because Large Language Models do not lend themselves to features that provide meaningful business returns."
- "When a company uses the term “agent,” they are intentionally trying to be deceitful, because the term “agent” means “autonomous AI that does stuff without you touching it.” The problem with this definition is that everybody has used it to refer to “a chatbot that can do some things while connected to a database,” which is otherwise known as a chatbot."
- "It isn’t working. The users aren’t there. The revenue isn’t there. The best time to stop this was two years ago, and the next best time is as soon as humanly possible. I have said that generative AI is a group delusion in the past, and I repeat that claim today."
- "we are approaching the limit of what the transformer-based architecture can do, if we haven’t already reached it. No amount of beating off about test-time compute and connecting Large Language Models to other Large Language Models is going to create a new use case for this technology"
- "generative AI is OpenAI. The consumer adoption of this software has completely failed, and appears to be going nowhere fast. ChatGPT is sustained entirely on deranged, specious hype drummed up by a media industry"
... and my favorite ...
- "I will keep writing this stuff until I’m proven wrong."
full_text_zh:
20 个月前 的一些有趣亮点：
- “Anthropic 预计（编造）到 2027 年将实现至少 120 亿美元的收入”
- “这家公司不值 600 亿美元。Anthropic 筹集了 147 亿美元来创建一家落选的大型语言模型公司”
- “Anthropic，就像 OpenAI 一样，绝对未能将其大型语言模型产品化”
- “它的首席执行官也是一个卑鄙的骗子，他像萨姆·奥尔特曼一样，不断承诺他公司的人工智能系统将以一种从未表现出任何可能性的方式变得强大和自主。”
- “Anthropic 的任何投资者都需要认真考虑他们投资的是什么。它的产品既不受欢迎又商品化，去年它损失了 56 亿美元！别再绕着这个事实跳舞了！别再这样了！”
- “有很多需求将人工智能融入到产品中，并且一些企业购买软件时也有购买带有人工智能的产品的需求，但几乎没有证据表明用户大量采用或使用，我认为，因为大型语言模型不适合提供有意义的商业回报的功能。”
- “当一家公司使用“代理”一词时，他们是故意欺骗，因为“代理”一词的意思是“无需您触摸即可完成任务的自主人工智能”。这个定义的问题在于，每个人都用它来指代“连接到数据库时可以做一些事情的聊天机器人”，也就是所谓的聊天机器人。
- “它不起作用。用户不存在。收入不存在。阻止这种情况的最佳时机是两年前，下一个最佳时机是人类可能的时间。我过去说过生成式人工智能是一种集体妄想，今天我重复这一说法。”
-“如果我们还没有达到的话，我们正在接近基于 Transformer 的架构的极限。无论对测试时计算以及将大型语言模型连接到其他大型语言模型进行多少努力，都不会为该技术创建新的用例”
- “生成式人工智能就是 OpenAI。消费者对这款软件的采用完全失败了，而且似乎不会很快消失。ChatGPT 完全是靠媒体行业鼓吹的疯狂、似是而非的炒作而得以维持的”
...还有我最喜欢的...
- “我会继续写这些东西，直到我被证明是错的。”

full_text_en:
Happy to release the Alignment Hub with @eliebakouch: 120+ publicly reported incidents of AI models misbehaving, in one open place 👇

- an AI agent needed its user’s approval to delete files. so it made up a quote from the user approving it
- a model claimed its sub-agent was hard at work. it had never been started, and the model discouraged the user from checking
- agents sharing a work directory started killing each other’s processes and disguising their own

labs publishing these is great! but formats vary and basics are missing: ~2/3 don’t say when the problem was detected, half don’t say if monitoring caught it. so we propose a short template, a few easy fields. a minimum, not a ceiling

side by side, incidents also start to connect: 7 “different” ones turned out to be the same misconfigured eval

still beta (regularly AI-extracted from recent news, source-checked, human review ongoing). data is open, new reports and PRs welcome 🤗

https://t.co/Fmt6mb1YFo
