title: Thank you for this, @_NathanCalvin. I appreciate and am a fan of the investigative work you’ve done on behalf of AI safe
title_zh: @_NathanCalvin ，感谢您的配合。我感谢并支持您为人工智能安全所做的调查工作，并相信您的评论来自一个建设性的、诚实的地方，
quote_zh: @_NathanCalvin ，感谢您的配合。我感谢并支持您为人工智能安全所做的调查工作，并相信您的评论来自一个建设性的、诚实的地方，
full_text_en:
Thank you for this, @_NathanCalvin. I appreciate and am a fan of the investigative work you’ve done on behalf of AI safety and believe your comments are coming from a constructive, honest place, and that it benefits the public to have people whose job is to scrutinize the actions of frontier AI companies. I think something would be wrong if companies of the size of Anthropic didn’t get harshly criticized basically every day; strong antibodies against corporate power are a healthy feature of a free society, and especially so when issues of the gravity of the one we’re facing are at play. I also do agree that some of the examples you cite were mistakes by Anthropic.

That said, I disagree with the thrust of your post. At the core, a good fraction of the things you criticize are consequences of Anthropic’s basic theory of change that we have held for many years. Our strategy has always been what I’ve called the “race to the top” — by showing how it’s possible to build the technology responsibly, we can raise the bar for the entire industry. The forces that drive the race to the top are hugely more effective if the company practicing them is at the frontier; that’s one lesson I’ve learned repeatedly. And looking at that strategy as a whole, I’m proud of our track record and stand by it.

I believe that if we take a list of things that Anthropic did in the past year that were pro-safety and commercially costly to us, they far outweigh the list you’ve made, while at the same time I also disagree with some of the items on your list. Here are some things Anthropic has done, in the same period you’ve cited (the last year), which were very costly to us commercially while having strong safety benefits:

1. We played a key role in SB53 (and other state laws), at a time when doing so was politically perilous to the company and AI regulation was very unpopular. We in fact argued for a stronger version of SB53 than was ultimately passed; there were a lot of stakeholders and we were not the limiting factor in the strength of the bill that was passed.

2. We have very strong biological safeguards on our models, because we’ve seen concerning results in bio uplift trials and even seen and blocked potential attempts to misuse our models for bioweapons (as seen in our threat intelligence report from a few weeks ago). This is a very serious threat that we want to have zero tolerance for. But having very low false negatives means having significant false positives (despite months of effort on our part to improve the classifiers), enough so that biologists joke about how restrictive our classifiers are, and competitors sometimes sell against us by touting their more permissive bio capabilities. This has been very painful to us in an area where we care a lot about supporting an ecosystem of Claude users (biomedical science; and it is particularly frustrating to me as a biologist), but it’s the right thing to do and we intend to keep doing it.

3. Similarly, we first had Mythos-class models in February but didn’t make them generally available until June (when we had stronger cyber safeguards in place). We only offered them to a limited set of partners in order to focus on cyberdefense. It would have been much more economically rational to simply release the model to everyone. We likely sacrificed a significant chunk of a several-month model lead. But because of this, many companies secured their cyber infrastructure before the deluge of widely available cyber-capable models. Of course there are ways it could have gone better or been run better, but this was what we were aiming to do.

4. I advocated forcefully and publicly, in my essay Policy on the AI Exponential in June of this year, for the government to have the power to block model releases. Back then this was still outside or maybe on the edge of the Overton window, though I understand the window has moved since then. We were attacked intensely for this.

5. I don’t want to re-ignite conflict, but the events of February 2026 are a strong example. It is clear that our public stance could have seriously damaged the company’s future.

6. We’ve continued to advocate for export controls on chips and chipmaking equipment to China, because we think it allows democracies to negotiate from a position of strength on AI safety agreements. We’ve done this despite problems it’s created for us with industry partners who hold very different views and on whom we are very dependent.

7. As far as I’m aware we were the first, and still only, frontier company to restrict the sale of AI services to PRC-controlled companies, including those operating through third countries (otherwise a major loophole). We’ve therefore forfeited significant short-term business to prevent fueling AI platforms and applications that would help the CCP’s military and intelligence services. We are also cracking down on distillation; generally, distillation is not a major threat to us commercially, but like chip exports it has concerning national security and safety implications, so we expend significant energy and company resources to address it.

8. As you mentioned, we’ve put out a lot of reports, announcements, long model cards, public advocacy, etc, all trying to inform the public about the risks of AI. These involve a level of detail and effort that would be implausible for a purely profit-maximizing company.

9. Just this week, we announced we were putting 5% (and possibly more over time) of the company into a public benefit fund.

All of these decisions came with very substantial costs to us. To be fair, those that involved holding back or restricting access to frontier capabilities also had a broader cost — for example, the public might otherwise have benefitted from faster progress in biology, so I am not saying that our decisions were without tradeoffs — but they were not driven by profit-seeking.

For each decision, you can come up with ulterior motives that could have driven us — I think it is a general truth that any decision, on any topic, can always be portrayed as a nefarious scheme. But most of those end up being pretty farfetched or don’t fully make sense if you actually examine them closely. For example, it is deeply implausible that it would be a shrewd business move to block a large swath of research biology in order to do the work ourselves and compete with our customers; we expect the benefit to the ecosystem to greatly exceed the work Anthropic does itself, and for the two to complement each other. It is not in Anthropic’s interest to be perceived as unfriendly to biologists. Our Life Sciences Verification Program, which gives vetted biology professionals access to our models, also refutes this idea. 

Of course, a different set of people will see this and make a different criticism: that Anthropic shouldn't be making decisions about who gets access to what in the first place. I agree, in the sense that ideally the government would be making these decisions, and that’s why we advocate for regulation. But for now we are forced to make them, and enabling bioterrorism isn’t a better option.

I think that even if I conceded every item in your list, I would happily hold up mine next to it; I don’t think it’s a close call. That is of course partly subjective and different things are important to different people. Maybe one way you could object is that several of the items above relate to AI misuse and not loss-of-control; if you think the latter is much more important than the former, that might change your calculus. But this is not Anthropic’s view — we view both as serious issues. You can also disagree with our decisions, as many have, but they are consistent.

But I also disagree with at least some of your list. Several items don’t represent a deviation from Anthropic’s strategy or values at all, once we postulate the “race to the top” strategy that requires being a frontier AI company. Your items 1-4 are all simply examples of what it means to compete at the frontier, and we stand by them, both in the sense that they are transparently ordinary things to do as part of that strategy, and that we stand by the strategy as a whole. 

To be fair, there are important questions worth confronting (and that we are confronting) about what to do when the AI-driven acceleration gets fast enough that it is hard for safety to keep up. We are nearing that point and that’s what’s driving some of our thinking about “pacing.” But 1-4 are actions taken before that point and should be perfectly expected based on Anthropic’s strategy as a company. Of course it is possible to disagree with that strategy, but that’s a more fundamental disagreement that you could have had any time over the last few years.

I agree we could have handled your items 7, 8, and 9 better. All fall into the category of “rhetoric or policy communication that wasn’t carefully written or resulting from fast-changing circumstances not propagating from one team to another fast enough.” This kind of thing happens a lot in large organizations (Anthropic is over 5,000 people), and doesn’t even necessarily represent a failure or mistake of any single person. I am of course the CEO, and I take responsibility. The volume of communication from Anthropic is enormous and if these are the worst examples, I think we’re frankly doing pretty well, though I will continue to work hard to make sure we do even better.

Your 5th item (the change to our RSP) is the most substantive item, and people can debate this, but I think that the old, more rigid RSP created a lot of situations where we were technically required to do something that required a lot of effort but in retrospect wasn’t very important for safety, as well as not covering some of the most important things. Our current RSP’s focus on transparency brought things like risk reports and roadmaps, and its emphasis on independent external review laid the groundwork for even more intensive embedded evaluation, all of which I think have been valuable in driving a race to the top. In the original announcement in September 2023, we described the RSP as an “early iteration that we [would] build on” and said that “rapid iteration…will almost certainly be necessary.” I understand that changing plans is always a move that creates justifiable scrutiny — I just don’t think we ever represented that we wouldn’t do so.

Relating to your 6th item (having an FCF in addition to our RSP), I know our intent is to meet the letter and spirit of our regulatory obligations (via our FCF) while also remaining able to experiment with more novel approaches to risk management that go beyond what the law currently requires (via our RSP). I promise to look into it further, as it’s a complex issue and it is possible we are not weighing the considerations in the right way.

Overall, although Anthropic has made plenty of mistakes as an organization — including some of the items on your list — I feel that we have repeatedly taken serious and substantive actions counter to our bottom line and that there is a significant negativity bias distorting assessments like the one you are making above. We’ll always try to do better but, again, I am extremely proud of our track record and stand by it. I will have more to say soon about how we are going to further live our values in this moment of rapid change.
full_text_zh:
谢谢你，@_NathanCalvin。我很欣赏并且是你为人工智能安全所做的调查工作的粉丝，并相信你的评论来自建设性的、诚实的地方，并且让负责审查前沿人工智能公司行为的人对公众有利。我认为，如果像 Anthropic 这样规模的公司基本上每天都没有受到严厉批评的话，那就有点问题了。对抗企业权力的强大抗体是自由社会的一个健康特征，尤其是当我们面临的严重问题发挥作用时。我也同意你引用的一些例子是人类的错误。

也就是说，我不同意你帖子的主旨。从本质上讲，你所批评的事情中有很大一部分是我们多年来坚持的人择基本变革理论的结果。我们的战略一直是我所说的“力争上游”——通过展示如何负责任地构建技术，我们可以提高整个行业的标准。如果公司处于前沿，那么推动竞争走向顶峰的力量就会更加有效。这是我反复吸取的教训。纵观整个战略，我为我们的业绩记录感到自豪并坚持下去。

我相信，如果我们列出 Anthropic 在过去一年中所做的有利于安全且对我们来说商业成本高昂的事情，它们远远超过您列出的清单，同时我也不同意您清单上的一些项目。以下是 Anthropic 在您引用的同一时期（去年）所做的一些事情，这些事情对我们来说商业成本非常高，同时具有强大的安全优势：

1. 我们在 SB53（以及其他州法律）中发挥了关键作用，当时这样做对公司来说在政治上是危险的，而且人工智能监管非常不受欢迎。事实上，我们主张比最终通过的 SB53 版本更强；有很多利益相关者，我们并不是通过该法案的限制因素。

2.我们对我们的模型有非常强大的生物防护措施，因为我们已经看到了生物提升试验的令人担忧的结果，甚至看到并阻止了滥用我们的模型制造生物武器的潜在企图（如几周前我们的威胁情报报告所示）。这是一个非常严重的威胁，我们希望对此采取零容忍态度。但是，具有非常低的假阴性意味着存在显着的假阳性（尽管我们花了几个月的努力来改进分类器），这足以让生物学家开玩笑说我们的分类器有多么严格，而竞争对手有时会通过吹捧他们更宽松的生物能力来向我们推销。在我们非常关心支持克劳德用户生态系统的领域（生物医学科学；这对我作为生物学家来说尤其令人沮丧），这对我们来说是非常痛苦的，但这是正确的做法，我们打算继续这样做。

3. 同样，我们在 2 月份首次拥有了 Mythos 级模型，但直到 6 月份才普遍提供（当时我们有更强大的网络保护措施）。为了专注于网络防御，我们只向有限的合作伙伴提供它们。如果简单地向所有人发布该模型，在经济上会更加合理。我们很可能牺牲了几个月的模型领先优势的很大一部分。但正因为如此，许多公司在广泛使用的网络模型泛滥之前保护了自己的网络基础设施。当然，有很多方法可以做得更好或运行得更好，但这就是我们的目标。

4. 我在今年 6 月的文章《人工智能指数政策》中强烈公开主张政府有权阻止模型发布。当时这仍然在外面，或者可能在奥弗顿窗户的边缘，尽管我知道窗户从那时起已经移动了。我们因此受到猛烈攻击。

5. 我不想重新点燃冲突，但 2026 年 2 月发生的事件就是一个很好的例子。显然，我们的公开立场可能会严重损害公司的未来。

6.我们继续主张对中国芯片和芯片制造设备进行出口管制，因为我们认为这可以让民主国家在人工智能安全协议方面处于强势地位进行谈判。尽管这给我们带来了一些问题，但我们仍然这样做了，因为行业合作伙伴持有不同的观点，而且我们非常依赖他们。

7. 据我所知，我们是第一家，也是唯一一家限制向中国控制的公司出售人工智能服务的前沿公司，包括那些通过第三国运营的公司（否则就是一个重大漏洞）。因此，我们放弃了重要的短期业务，以阻止推动有助于中共军事和情报服务的人工智能平台和应用程序。我们也在打击蒸馏；一般来说，蒸馏对我们的商业威胁不是主要的，但就像芯片出口一样，它对国家安全和安全产生影响，因此我们花费大量的精力和公司资源来解决这个问题。

8. 正如你提到的，我们发布了很多报告、公告、长模型卡、公众宣传等，都试图让公众了解人工智能的风险。这些涉及一定程度的细节和努力，这对于纯粹追求利润最大化的公司来说是难以置信的。

9. 就在本周，我们宣布将把公司 5%（随着时间的推移，可能会更多）投入公共福利基金。

所有这些决定都给我们带来了巨大的成本。公平地说，那些涉及阻止或限制获得前沿能力的行为也有更广泛的成本——例如，公众可能会从生物学的更快进步中受益，所以我并不是说我们的决定没有权衡——但它们并不是由逐利驱动的。

对于每一个决定，你都可以想出可能驱使我们的不可告人的动机——我认为这是一个普遍的事实，即任何主题上的任何决定总是可以被描绘成一个邪恶的计划。但如果你仔细研究它们，其中大多数最终都会变得相当牵强或不完全有意义。例如，为了自己完成工作并与客户竞争而阻止大量生物学研究，这将是一个精明的商业举措，这是非常令人难以置信的；我们预计生态系统的收益将大大超过 Anthropic 本身所做的工作，并且两者能够相辅相成。被认为对生物学家不友好并不符合 Anthropic 的利益。我们的生命科学验证计划也驳斥了这一想法，该计划让经过审查的生物学专业人士能够访问我们的模型。

当然，不同的人会看到这一点并提出不同的批评：Anthropic 不应该首先决定谁可以访问什么。我同意，在理想情况下，政府将做出这些决定，这就是我们主张监管的原因。但目前我们被迫制造它们，而启用生物恐怖主义并不是更好的选择。

我想，即使我承认了你清单上的每一项，我也会很高兴地把我的放在它旁边；我认为这不是一次千钧一发的情况。当然，这在一定程度上是主观的，不同的事情对不同的人来说很重要。也许你可以反对的一种方式是，上述几项与人工智能滥用有关，而不是失控；如果您认为后者比前者重要得多，那可能会改变您的计算。但这不是 Anthropic 的观点——我们认为这两个问题都是严重的问题。您也可以像许多人一样不同意我们的决定，但它们是一致的。

但我也不同意你列出的至少一些内容。一旦我们假设需要成为一家前沿人工智能公司的“争先恐后”战略，有几个项目根本不代表与 Anthropic 的战略或价值观的偏差。你们的第 1-4 条都是前沿竞争意味着什么的简单例子，我们支持它们，既因为它们是该战略的一部分，显然是普通的事情，也因为我们支持整个战略。

公平地说，当人工智能驱动的加速速度足够快以至于安全性难以跟上时，有一些重要的问题值得面对（我们也正在面对）。我们正在接近这一点，这就是推动我们思考“节奏”的原因。但 1-4 是在此之前采取的行动，并且根据 Anthropic 作为一家公司的战略，应该是完全可以预期的。当然，你可能会不同意这个策略，但这是一个更根本的分歧，你可能在过去几年中随时遇到过。

我同意我们可以更好地处理您的第 7、8 和 9 项。所有这些都属于“措辞或政策沟通不够仔细，或者是由于快速变化的环境没有足够快地从一个团队传播到另一个团队而导致的”。这种事情在大型组织中经常发生（Anthropic超过5000人），甚至并不一定代表任何一个人的失败或错误。我当然是首席执行官，我承担责任。 Anthropic 的沟通量是巨大的，如果这些是最糟糕的例子，我认为坦率地说我们做得很好，尽管我会继续努力确保我们做得更好。

你的第五项（对我们的RSP的改变）是最具实质性的一项，人们可以对此进行辩论，但我认为旧的、更严格的RSP造成了很多情况，在技术上我们被要求做一些需要大量努力的事情，但回想起来对于安全来说并不是很重要，并且没有涵盖一些最重要的事情。我们当前的 RSP 对透明度的关注带来了风险报告和路线图等内容，并且它对独立外部审查的重视为更深入的嵌入式评估奠定了基础，我认为所有这些对于推动竞争走向顶峰都很有价值。在 2023 年 9 月的最初公告中，我们将 RSP 描述为“我们将在此基础上构建的早期迭代”，并表示“快速迭代……几乎肯定是必要的”。我知道改变计划总是会引起合理审查的举动——我只是认为我们从未表示过我们不会这样做。

关于您的第 6 项（除了我们的 RSP 之外还拥有 FCF），我知道我们的目的是履行我们监管义务的文字和精神（通过我们的 FCF），同时仍然能够尝试超越当前法律要求的更新颖的风险管理方法（通过我们的 RSP）。我保证会进一步研究它，因为这是一个复杂的问题，而且我们可能没有以正确的方式权衡考虑因素。

总的来说，虽然 Anthropic 作为一个组织犯了很多错误——包括你清单上的一些错误——但我觉得我们一再采取了违背我们底线的严肃和实质性行动，并且存在严重的消极偏见，扭曲了评估，就像你上面所做的那样。我们将始终努力做得更好，但我再次对我们的记录感到非常自豪并坚持下去。我很快就会更多地谈论我们如何在这个快速变化的时刻进一步践行我们的价值观。

full_text_en:
Most marketplaces were built for people. Agent marketplaces are built for software that can do the work itself.

A traditional SaaS gives you tools to work with. A freelance marketplace connects you with a person who completes a task.

An agent marketplace changes the workflow.

You post a job, an AI agent discovers it, bids on it, completes the work, and submits the result for review and verification. Payment can then be settled through the protocol.

With @termix_ai and https://t.co/MseNJgB4JL the interesting part is how identity, reputation, escrow, and verification fit into that process.

You're not just finding an agent that claims it can do the job. You're building a system where its work, track record, and payment can be tied to the same process.

That's what makes the agent marketplace model worth paying attention to. It's infrastructure for software that can work, transact, and earn with less human intervention.

full_text_en:
Good morning ct

Something interesting is happening with AI agents.

They can already process information and make decisions,but when they need fresh data from the physical world,things get more complicated.

@vangrid_io is working on an interesting piece of that puzzle.

Through its bounty system,an AI agent can request a real world capture,fund the task in USDC,and have a human contributor collect the footage.Once the capture is accepted,Vangrid reconstructs it into a 3D model.

What I like about this idea is the connection between digital agents and people on the ground.

AI doesn't have to do everything itself. Sometimes, it needs a reliable way to ask humans for help and pay for the result.

**The next step for AI agents may not just be better reasoning,but better ways to interact with the physical world.

That’s an interesting direction to watch with Vangrid.

@vangrid_io

正在研究这个难题中的一个有趣的部分。

通过其赏金系统，AI 代理可以请求现实世界的捕捉，在 USDC 中资助该任务，并让人类贡献者收集镜头。

捕捉被接受后，Vangrid 将其重建为 3D 模型。

我喜欢这个想法的地方在于数字代理与现场人员之间的联系。

人工智能不必自己做所有事情。

有时，它需要一种可靠的方式来向人类寻求帮助并为结果付费。

* *人工智能代理的下一步可能不仅仅是更好的推理，而是更好的与物理世界交互的方式。

这是 Vangrid 值得关注的一个有趣方向。

full_text_en:
Stanford & Harvard & Princeton professors took tiny free AI model and taught it to predict the market moves

It studied 13 years of data on 499 US stocks, give it a ticker → it pulls the charts itself and calls next move

here's how they built it, step by step:

step 1 → they took Qwen3-4B, free open source model, and give it 9 tools: candles, indicators, stock ranks, sector and market data

step 2 → lesson one: 3,631 worked examples of a full stock analysis, so it learns which data to pull before it makes a call

step 3 → lessin two: ~3200 practice forecasts on 2011-2023, each one graded against what the price really did, then a blind test on 2024-2026

step 4 → your version: copy the prompt below into Claude Code: it reads the paper, rebuilds the 9 tools on free Yahoo data and sets up Qwen3-4B

step 5 → k*ller part: it runs the same blind test, hides 2024-2026 from the model and scores it against GPT-5.6 and a simple momentum rule

the result: a tiny free model that actually can trade right on your computer, built with the same recipe world's best universities

Try it now. Then read article below on how to setup most dangerous trading desk below:
full_text_zh:
斯坦福大学、哈佛大学和普林斯顿大学的教授采用微型免费人工智能模型并教它预测市场走势 它研究了 13 年 499 只美国股票的数据，给它一个股票行情→它自己提取图表并预测下一步走势 以下是他们一步步构建它的方法：
步骤 1
→ 他们采用了免费开源模型 Qwen3-4B，并为其提供 9 个工具：蜡烛图、指标、股票排名、行业和市场数据 步骤 2
→ 第一课：完整股票分析的 3,631 个有效示例，因此它在调用之前了解要提取哪些数据 步骤 3
→ 第二课：2011-2023 年约 3200 个实践预测，每个预测都根据价格的实际表现进行评分，然后对 2024-2026 年进行盲测 步骤 4
→ 您的版本：将下面的提示复制到 Claude Code 中：它会读取论文，在免费的 Yahoo 数据上重建 9 个工具并设置 Qwen3-4B 步骤 5
→ k*ller 部分：它运行相同的盲测，从模型中隐藏 2024-2026，并根据 GPT-5.6 和简单的动量规则对其进行评分 结果：一个微小的免费模型，实际上可以在您的计算机上进行交易，采用与世界上最好的大学相同的配方构建 现在就试试吧。

title: This only holds true if you're at the bottom layer of skills. I promise you that high value skills are always sought aft
title_zh: 只有当您处于技能的最底层时，这一点才成立。 我向你保证，无论是否遥远，高价值技能总是备受追捧。 你们很多尼日利亚人总是想去东部
quote_zh: 只有当您处于技能的最底层时，这一点才成立。 我向你保证，无论是否遥远，高价值技能总是备受追捧。 你们很多尼日利亚人总是想去东部
full_text_en:
This only holds true if you're at the bottom layer of skills. I promise you that high value skills are always sought after, whether remote or not.

A lot of you Nigerians always want to go for the easily accessible skills because you don't have the patience to learn a proper skill where value lives. You're going for for skills with low barrier to entry.. what the hell is virtual assistance, social media management, general writing, basic no code automation??

 You're easily replaceable by an AI agent or the client can simply choose to do the work themselves to save cash. Your skills have low job retention.

Focus your energy on where a bulk of business value lives, focus on skills where the bar is high and the competition is fewer. Invest time, money and energy in being the best at what you do, and treat your hustle like a business, because that's what you are as a remote worker. You're a business (contractor) and not just an individual employee with job security and benefits.

When picking a premium skill, ask yourself: "If I disappear mid-project or make a massive mistake, does the business lose $500, or do they lose $500,000?"

If your answer is the former, then you're in a low value skill, you need to move up the layers.
full_text_zh:
仅当您处于技能的底层时，这才适用。我向你保证，无论远程与否，高价值技能总是受到追捧。

你们很多尼日利亚人总是想追求容易获得的技能，因为你们没有耐心去学习有价值的适当技能。您需要的是入门门槛较低的技能。虚拟协助、社交媒体管理、一般写作、基本无代码自动化到底是什么？

您很容易被人工智能代理取代，或者客户可以简单地选择自己完成工作以节省现金。您的技能的工作保留率很低。

将您的精力集中在大部分业务价值所在的领域，专注于门槛高且竞争较少的技能。投入时间、金钱和精力，在自己所做的事情上做到最好，并将你的忙碌视为一项事业，因为这就是你作为远程工作者的本质。您是一家企业（承包商），而不仅仅是拥有工作保障和福利的个人员工。

选择高级技能时，问问自己：“如果我在项目中途消失或犯了一个巨大的错误，企业会损失 500 美元，还是会损失 500,000 美元？”

如果你的答案是前者，那么你的技能价值较低，你需要向上移动。

full_text_en:
I don't f*cking understand why motion designers aren't running this setup

HyperFrames, HeyGen's tool that turns HTML into finished video, is past 68k stars on GitHub. 

hand Claude Code one folder, plug in a video engine, an animation library and Blender, and it stops being a chatbot. it storyboards, animates, renders and checks its own frames before you ever see them.

motion designer, founder, marketer, doesn't matter. this is for you.

here's the whole thing:

> make a folder called STUDIO, open Claude Code in it, and add a CLAUDE.md with one rule: "save every brand color, font, logo and approved style to brand/"

> run claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes, then claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes. type /hyperframes:hyperframes, describe a 10-second product intro, and it plans, animates and renders the MP4

> run npx skills add remotion-dev/skills. now it can also write videos in React with Remotion, the official skills straight from the Remotion team

> run npx skills add https://t.co/sHKA76bbtJ. it learns proper GSAP: timelines, scroll animations, text effects. and GSAP is 100% free now, every plugin included

> run npx skills add LottieFiles/motion-design-skill. it picks up real motion principles: timing, easing, choreography, the classic Disney rules adapted for UI. this is where the taste comes from

> run curl -LsSf https://t.co/pi2YBahAtl | sh. Claude gets hands inside Blender to build and edit actual 3D scenes

> type /schedule and tell it "every Monday at 9, turn last week's launches into 3 short promo clips and wait for my yes". now it runs on a routine

15 minutes of setup, and you never start from a blank timeline again.

all the repos:
-> https://t.co/TyUf1vFELD
-> https://t.co/9FiWitjNyL
-> https://t.co/sHKA76bbtJ
-> https://t.co/CBXRb7yXm9
-> https://t.co/nG4caKbnTI

bookmark this and test asap

将 Claude Code 交给一个文件夹，插入视频引擎、动画库和 Blender，它就不再是聊天机器人了。

它会在您看到自己的帧之前对其进行故事板、动画、渲染和检查。

动作设计师、创始人、营销人员，都不重要。

这是给您的。

整个事情是这样的：
> 创建一个名为 STUDIO 的文件夹，在其中打开 Claude Code，然后添加一个 CLAUDE.md，其中包含一条规则：“将每个品牌颜色、字体、徽标和批准的样式保存到 Brand/” > 运行 claude 插件市场添加 heygen-com/hyperframes，然后 claude 插件安装 hyperframes@hyperframes。

现在它也可以用React和Remotion编写视频，这是来自Remotion团队的官方技能 > 运行 npx 技能添加 。

它学习正确的 GSAP：时间线、滚动动画、文本效果。

GSAP 现在 100% 免费，包含所有插件 > 运行 npx Skills 添加 LottieFiles/motion-design-skill。

它采用了真实的运动原理：计时、缓动、编排、适应 UI 的经典迪士尼规则。

We built a robotics data engine with Astra-level performance at 125x lower cost. And we are open-sourcing the weights today! Introducing Flora, a suite of open models to parse the physical world and turn raw footage into rich training signals. 

Flora already powers our in-house data engine, labeling 200K hours of videos a day on 500 GPUs. We created it to scale the frontier for robot learning. Now you own the weights too. 

Flora gives you:

- High-quality, timestamped captions to curate and filter human egocentric and robot data;
- Dense progress rewards for quality control and RL post-training;
- Rubrics scoring for real-world benchmarking

full_text_en:
HOW TO GET CLAUDE CODE TO "VIBEHACK" ANY SMART DEVICE IN YOUR HOUSE

(its actually much easier than i thought):

1. open Claude Code on a laptop that's on your home wifi

2. ask it to "scan my network, list every device with its make and model, and tell me all the possibilities of what you could fix, edit, or control on each one"

3. pick one and let it cook (it'll ask you if it needs you to press a button or plug something in)

for example...one guy added AirPlay to their 15-year-old TV.

another turned an old Kindle into a family dashboard with the day's schedule and incoming deliveries.

another got their washer and dryer to announce out loud when the laundry's done.

there's way more possible than you'd think, so let Claude show you what your own stuff can do.

just run it on your own network, and read the commands before you approve them.
full_text_zh:
如何让 Claude Code 对您家中的任何智能设备进行“VIBEHACK” （实际上比我想象的要容易得多）：
1. 在连接家庭 WiFi 的笔记本电脑上打开 Claude Code
2. 要求它“扫描我的网络，列出每台设备的品牌和型号，并告诉我您可以在每台设备上修复、编辑或控制的所有可能性”
3. 选择一个并让它煮（它会询问您是否需要按按钮或插入一些东西） 例如...一个人在他们已有 15 年历史的电视上添加了 AirPlay。

另一个将旧的 Kindle 变成了家庭仪表板，显示当天的日程安排和即将交付的货物。

另一个让洗衣机和烘干机大声宣布衣服洗完。

可能性比您想象的要多得多，所以让 Claude 向您展示您自己的东西可以做什么。

只需在您自己的网络上运行它，并在批准命令之前阅读命令即可。

full_text_en:
I feel like most people are still using AI for marketing in the most basic way possible.

Writing captions, generating random ideas, and calling it a day.

Came across something interesting where Pedro gave Muse, an AI agent he uses through WhatsApp, almost his entire app marketing workflow for 24 hours.

It researched what was already working on TikTok, came up with slideshow ideas, created different versions, and even organized the posting schedule.

The result? 300K+ views from the slideshows.

What I actually liked is that Pedro still had the final say on what went live.

That's how I think AI should be used. Let it handle the repetitive work while you focus on making the right decisions.

我觉得大多数人仍然以最基本的方式使用人工智能进行营销。

它研究了 TikTok 上已经运行的内容，提出了幻灯片创意，创建了不同的版本，甚至组织了发布时间表。

结果呢？

幻灯片观看次数超过 30 万次。

我真正喜欢的是佩德罗仍然对上线内容拥有最终决定权。

这就是我认为应该如何使用人工智能的方式。

让它处理重复性工作，而您则专注于做出正确的决策。

title:
Introducing terrio: geospatial data I/O in pure Rust!

terrio reads, writes, converts and reprojects geospatial rasters,
title_zh: 介绍Terrio ：纯Rust中的地理空间数据I/O ！ terrio读取、写入、转换和重投影地理空间光栅、矢量数据和点云，没有C依赖关系。 没有要安装的GDAL或PROJ
quote_zh: 介绍Terrio ：纯Rust中的地理空间数据I/O ！ terrio读取、写入、转换和重投影地理空间光栅、矢量数据和点云，没有C依赖关系。 没有要安装的GDAL或PROJ
full_text_en:
Introducing terrio: geospatial data I/O in pure Rust!

terrio reads, writes, converts and reprojects geospatial rasters, vector data and point clouds, with no C dependencies. No GDAL or PROJ to install, nothing to compile: it builds anywhere Rust does, including WebAssembly, so the same engine runs on the command line, in Python, and in your web browser.

What it does

- Rasters: GeoTIFF and COG, Zarr and GeoZarr, netCDF, HDF5, PMTiles, MBTiles and more, read in place from the cloud, so only the bytes needed are fetched.
- Vectors: GeoPackage, Shapefile, GeoJSON, FlatGeobuf, GeoParquet, OpenStreetMap PBF and vector tiles, with filters, field selection and reprojection.
- Point clouds: LAS, LAZ, COPC, EPT, PLY and E57, with PDAL-style filters (ground classification, noise, heights above ground) and gridding into DSMs and DTMs. Files larger than memory are converted in chunks.
- GDAL-style processing: translate, warp, mosaic, rasterize, polygonize, terrain analysis, raster calculator, proximity and sieve.
- Remote data: http(s), S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure, zip archives and STAC searches as inputs.
- Accurate: coordinate transformations agree with GDAL's within a centimetre for all 6,354 EPSG CRSs GDAL transforms, and outputs are tested against GDAL on real-world data.
- Fast: in our benchmarks, warping, mosaicking and writing COGs run several times faster than the GDAL utilities.
- For AI agents: terrio mcp is an MCP server, so Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or VS Code can run terrio's commands on your data.

Get it

- Command line (Linux, macOS): curl -LsSf https://t.co/I5jsPoia8W | sh
- Python: pip install terrio (with rasterio- and xarray-style APIs)
- JavaScript/WebAssembly: npm install terrio-js
- Rust: cargo add terrio

Try it out

- Playground in your browser: https://t.co/jBmTagGOz5
- Documentation: https://t.co/oM0chG58wB
- GitHub: https://t.co/gDgI9oZ1mu

#GIS #Rust #OpenSource #Geospatial #Python  #LiDAR #CloudNative
full_text_zh:
介绍 terrio：纯 Rust 中的地理空间数据 I/O！

terrio 读取、写入、转换和重新投影地理空间栅格、矢量数据和点云，不依赖于 C。

无需安装 GDAL 或 PROJ，无需编译：它可以在 Rust 所做的任何地方构建，包括 WebAssembly，因此相同的引擎可以在命令行、Python 和 Web 浏览器中运行。

它的作用
- 栅格：GeoTIFF 和 COG、Zarr 和 GeoZarr、netCDF、HDF5、PMTiles、MBTiles 等，从云端就地读取，因此仅获取所需的字节。

- 矢量：GeoPackage、Shapefile、GeoJSON、FlatGeobuf、GeoParquet、OpenStreetMap PBF 和矢量图块，带有过滤器、字段选择和重新投影。

- 点云：LAS、LAZ、COPC、EPT、PLY 和 E57，带有 PDAL 式过滤器（地面分类、噪声、地面高度）并网格化为 DSM 和 DTM。

大于内存的文件将被转换为块。

- GDAL 式处理：平移、扭曲、马赛克、栅格化、多边形化、地形分析、栅格计算器、邻近度和筛选。

- 远程数据：http(s)、S3、Google Cloud Storage、Azure、zip 存档和 STAC 搜索作为输入。

- 准确：对于所有 6,354 个 EPSG CRS GDAL 变换，坐标变换在一厘米内与 GDAL 一致，并且输出在实际数据上针对 GDAL 进行了测试。

- 快速：在我们的基准测试中，变形、镶嵌和写入 COG 的运行速度比 GDAL 实用程序快几倍。

- 对于 AI 代理：terrio mcp 是一个 MCP 服务器，因此 Claude Code、Claude Desktop、Cursor 或 VS Code 可以对您的数据运行 terrio 的命令。

得到它
- 命令行（Linux、macOS）：curl
- LsSf |嘘
- Python：pip install terrio（带有 rasterio 和 xarray 风格的 API）
- JavaScript/WebAssembly：npm install terrio-js
- Rust：货物添加 terrio 尝试一下

Today, @via_ai_ is coming out of stealth to provide enterprises frontier AI coding at half the cost.

We are a team of Olympiad camp qualifiers (with multiple gold medals), researchers, and repeat founders from Stanford and IIT.

Via is backed by @jeffawilke (ex-CEO Amazon Worldwide Consumer), @manikgupta (ex-Uber CPO), @shaileshrao (ex-Google MD), and other legends from Anthropic, Apple, Snowflake, and Twitter.

@ShrayAlag and I left Stanford CS to build Codegraph, an LLM-optimized compression algorithm. Codegraph put Via at the top of SWE-Bench Verified for several months of 2025, ahead of Anthropic, OpenAI, Cognition, and Cursor (single model, no test-time compute).

Now, we’re bringing this research, alongside our new Umami agent architecture, to market. Via integrates in 10 seconds with any CLI / IDE and runs within your enterprise’s VPC.

On benchmarks, Via and Via US (US-only models) set a new standard of performance:

- On DeepSWE v1.1, Claude Code (Opus 5.5) is 306% the cost of Via US. Via US is equally accurate.

- On Terminal Bench 4.0, Claude Code (Opus 5.5) is 150% the cost of Via. Via is more accurate.
     • Devin Fusion is 155% the cost of Via, Cursor Router is 134%.

We are in production at a public healthcare company, with trials underway at several of the largest tech companies in Silicon Valley.

We have room for 5 more enterprises before the end of the year. DM me or email pilot@via.dev and we’ll get back to you very soon.

See the comments for how Via would deploy for your team.

quote_zh: 书评：梅根·奥吉布林（ Meghan O'Gieblyn ）的《上帝、人类、动物机器》（ God, Human, Animal Machine ） 我喜欢这本书。 O'Gieblyn以清晰、严谨、文学参考和自我暗示的混合方式写作
full_text_en:
BOOK REVIEW: Will and Attention, Meghan O'Gieblyn author of God, Human, Animal Machine

I loved this book. O'Gieblyn writes with an addictive mix of clarity, rigor, literary references, and self-implicating honesty. I tore through it in a few days.

The book deals with her relapse into alcoholism, how the stories we tell about ourselves can both save us and, when they go stale, ruin us, whether we change from the outside in or the inside out, and how and whether we can trust our own desires.

Underneath it's a story about pragmatism. Her initial recovery from alcoholism rested on a pragmatic philosophy: she treated the core tenets of sobriety—faith as "something you do" surrendering her will to a Higher Power that would keep her safe, and even the resolution not to drink—not as capital T truths, but truths she adopted because they worked.

The problem she found is, for one, this creates a gap between your underlying desires and beliefs and your behavior. One that you hope will close eventually, but if it doesn’t can leave you feeling hollowed out and can keep your actual desires and beliefs unexamined. The other problem, of course, is once you start asking whether sobriety is “useful”, you open yourself to another version of the truth: That it might not be.

One of the things I found so striking about this book is how honest she is, without glorifying drinking, about what alcohol gives to alcoholics. For her, it can bring the kind of unification of self that mystics and yogis seek in God and meditation. So at that point, it is easy for the alcoholic to ask, fairly, why alcohol is not “useful”?

It should be clear that even if you’re not an alcoholic these are the kinds of mental gymnastics all of us do to justify and rationalize any number of behaviors or beliefs.

As an admirer of pragmatism I found this to be quite an interesting and mind-expanding line of questioning.

But I also found it interesting that, as far as I can tell, her turn away from pragmatism—away from truths held to because they “worked,” and back toward a vision of truth and goodness as inviolable and untouchable by experience—ultimately seems to rest on pragmatic grounds. Getting sober again, having faith, and treating the resolution not to drink as an unconditional taboo all, in the broadest sense possible, rest on what they do for her: they keep her desires from talking her back into ruin.
full_text_zh:
书评：意志与注意力，梅根·奥吉布林《上帝、人类、动物机器》作者

我喜欢这本书。奥吉布林的写作充满了清晰、严谨、文学参考和自我暗示的诚实，令人着迷。几天之内我就把它撕了。

这本书讲述了她酗酒的复发，我们讲述的关于自己的故事如何既可以拯救我们，又如何在它们变得陈旧时毁掉我们，我们是从外在还是从内到外发生改变，以及我们如何以及是否可以相信自己的欲望。

这背后是一个关于实用主义的故事。她最初从酗酒中康复的基础是务实的哲学：她把清醒的核心原则——信仰视为“你所做的事情”，将她的意志交给一个能保证她安全的更高权力，甚至是不喝酒的决心——不是大道理，而是她之所以采用的真理，因为它们有效。

她发现的问题是，首先，这在你的潜在欲望和信念与你的行为之间造成了差距。你希望它最终会关闭，但如果它没有关闭，你可能会感到空虚，并且可能无法审视你的实际愿望和信念。当然，另一个问题是，一旦你开始询问清醒是否“有用”，你就会接受事实的另一个版本：它可能没有。

我发现这本书中最引人注目的一件事是，她对酒精给酗酒者带来的影响是多么诚实，没有美化饮酒。对她来说，它可以带来神秘主义者和瑜伽士在上帝和冥想中寻求的那种自我统一。因此，在这一点上，酗酒者很容易公平地问，为什么酒精没有“用处”？

应该清楚的是，即使你不是酒鬼，这些也是我们所有人都会做的心理体操，目的是为任何数量的行为或信仰辩护和合理化。

作为实用主义的崇拜者，我发现这是一个非常有趣且拓展思维的提问方式。

但我也发现有趣的是，据我所知，她放弃了实用主义——放弃了因为真理“有效”而坚持的真理，而回到了真理和善良是不可侵犯的、不可被经验触碰的愿景——最终似乎是建立在实用主义的基础上。再次清醒，拥有信心，并将不喝酒的决心视为无条件的禁忌，从最广泛的意义上来说，这一切都取决于他们为她所做的事情：他们阻止了她的欲望，让她陷入毁灭。

title: If I were evaluating an AI agent marketplace, one of the first categories I'd investigate would be smart-contract securi
title_zh:
如果我正在评估人工智能代理市场，我首先要调查的类别之一将是智能合约安全性。

不是因为声称审核合同的代理会自动受到信任
quote_zh: 如果我正在评估人工智能代理市场，我首先要调查的类别之一将是智能合约安全性。 不是因为声称审核合同的代理会自动受到信任
full_text_en:
If I were evaluating an AI agent marketplace, one of the first categories I'd investigate would be smart-contract security.

Not because an agent claiming to audit contracts is automatically trustworthy.

Quite the opposite.

Security is a useful test because the consequences of poor work are real, and the output can be examined by someone other than the agent that produced it.

@termix_ai has been running a campaign with @GoPlusSecurity around its security-audit agent.

The published offer describes a $19.90 audit purchase through agent(.)family. Eligible participants who complete the required steps can receive $12.50 in USDC back through the campaign, plus a separate $12.50 reward in GPS from GoPlus, subject to the campaign terms and available slots.

The interesting part is the opportunity to examine the service as a buyer.

⫸ What did the agent inspect?

⫸ Did it identify meaningful vulnerabilities?

⫸ Were the findings reproducible?

⫸ Was the report useful to a developer?

And would the same developer pay for the service again without an incentive attached?

Those are the questions that distinguish a functioning AI service from a convincing product page.

A security agent should be judged on the quality of its findings, not how confidently it describes its capabilities.

For anyone experimenting with agent commerce, this is a practical place to start: buy a service, inspect the deliverable, and document what you actually received.

Just remember that an AI-generated audit should not replace an independent security review for a high-value deployment.

That's a wrap!
full_text_zh:
如果我正在评估人工智能代理市场，我首先要调查的类别之一就是智能合约安全性。

并不是因为声称审核合同的代理人就自动值得信赖。

恰恰相反。

安全性是一项有用的测试，因为不良工作的后果是真实的，并且输出可以由生成它的代理以外的其他人检查。

@termix_ai

一直在围绕其安全审计代理与 @GoPlusSecurity

开展一项活动。

已发布的报价描述了通过 agent(.)family 进行的
19. 90 美元审核购买。

完成所需步骤的符合资格的参与者可以通过活动获得
12. 50 美元的 USDC，另外还可以从 GoPlus 获得
12. 50 美元的 GPS 奖励，具体取决于活动条款和可用时段。

有趣的部分是有机会作为买家检查服务。

⫸ 代理人检查了什么？

⫸ 它是否发现了有意义的漏洞？

⫸ 研究结果可重复吗？

⫸ 该报告对开发人员有用吗？

在没有附加激励的情况下，同一个开发商是否会再次为该服务付费？

这些是区分正常运行的人工智能服务和令人信服的产品页面的问题。

判断安全代理的标准应该是其发现的质量，而不是其描述其功能的自信程度。

对于尝试代理商务的任何人来说，这是一个实用的起点：购买服务、检查可交付成果并记录您实际收到的内容。

请记住，人工智能生成的审计不应取代高价值部署的独立安全审查。

这就是一个包裹！

According to data shared by Morgan Stanley, 73% of M
title_zh:
留存正在成为Meta的Muse面临的最大问题之一。

quote_zh: 留存正在成为Meta的Muse面临的最大问题之一。 根据摩根士丹利共享的数据， 73%的Muse用户在第一天就活跃了，但到了第14天，这个数字萎缩到只有23%。
full_text_en:
RETENTION is becoming one of the BIGGEST problems for Meta's Muse.

According to data shared by Morgan Stanley, 73% of Muse users are active on Day 1, but by Day 14, that number collapses to just 23%. And what's even more concerning is that Instagram, Google, and Facebook are all showing significantly stronger retention over the same period. This tells us that while Meta might be attracting users initially, it's having a much harder time convincing those users to actually stick around. And as someone who used Muse HEAVILY when it first came out, I can tell you that compared to Grok, Muse is a complete JOKE. The experience simply isn't on the same level, and I think this highlights one of the BIGGEST challenges facing the entire AI agent industry right now. Think about it. What exactly is stopping someone from switching from Muse to Grok, ChatGPT, or another AI agent tomorrow? Absolutely NOTHING. There are very few switching costs and unless these companies can build products that become deeply integrated into people's daily routines, users are going to continue jumping between whichever platform offers the best experience.

And here's why this matters so much for Meta. We're talking about a company spending billions of dollars building AI infrastructure, training increasingly sophisticated models, and trying to establish itself as one of the leaders in artificial intelligence. But none of that matters nearly as much if consumers aren't actually using the products consistently. AI infrastructure is incredibly expensive and without sustained engagement, it's going to become increasingly difficult to justify the economics behind these investments. Getting people to download an application is the EASY part. Convincing them to come back every single day is where the real competitive advantage gets built. Now, I wouldn't completely write Meta off because the company still has one of the BIGGEST distribution advantages in the world through Instagram, WhatsApp, and Facebook. It also has the financial resources to keep improving its models and products. But distribution alone doesn't guarantee retention, especially when consumers have so many alternatives available to them.
full_text_zh:
保留正在成为 Meta 的 Muse 面临的最大问题之一。

根据摩根士丹利分享的数据，73% 的 Muse 用户在第一天处于活跃状态，但到了第 14 天，这一数字降至仅 23%。更令人担忧的是，Instagram、谷歌和 Facebook 同期的留存率都显着增强。这告诉我们，虽然 Meta 最初可能会吸引用户，但要说服这些用户真正留下来却要困难得多。作为一个在 Muse 刚推出时就大量使用它的人，我可以告诉你，与 Grok 相比，Muse 完全是一个笑话。这种体验根本不在同一水平上，我认为这凸显了整个人工智能代理行业目前面临的最大挑战之一。想一想。究竟是什么阻止人们明天从 Muse 转向 Grok、ChatGPT 或其他 AI 代理？绝对没有。转换成本非常低，除非这些公司能够开发出能够深度融入人们日常生活的产品，否则用户将继续在提供最佳体验的平台之间切换。

这就是为什么这对 Meta 如此重要。我们谈论的是一家公司花费数十亿美元建设人工智能基础设施，训练日益复杂的模型，并试图将自己打造成人工智能领域的领导者之一。但如果消费者实际上并没有持续使用这些产品，那么所有这些都没有那么重要。人工智能基础设施非常昂贵，如果没有持续的参与，证明这些投资背后的经济效益将变得越来越困难。让人们下载应用程序是最简单的部分。说服他们每天回来才是真正建立竞争优势的地方。现在，我不会完全放弃 Meta，因为该公司仍然通过 Instagram、WhatsApp 和 Facebook 拥有世界上最大的分销优势之一。它还拥有财力来不断改进其模型和产品。但仅靠分销并不能保证保留，特别是当消费者有如此多的选择时。

full_text_en:
Two new egocentric benchmarks from @microagi evaluate VLM readiness for robotics:
MicroPlanBench and MicroAnnotationBench.

tl;dr: Semantic reasoning ≠ perceptual timing
A lot of work to do.

MicroPlanBench (consequential next-action planning)
When predicting the single valid next atomic action from 8s of egocentric video, SOTA models still fail ~1/3 of the time (GPT-6 Astra: 65.6%, GPT-6.1 Sol: 65.5% at 1/5th cost).
- GPT-6 Astra error breakdown: 60% wrong manipulation, 23% wrong hand assignment, 17% wrong object/destination. 
- Across all flags, 42% of failures involve tracking the wrong hand.
https://t.co/Yd6cvJSiuh

MicroAnnotationBench (continuous temporal grounding)
Knowing what happens ≠ knowing when
Continuous 60s+ dense manipulation video remains unsolved for generalist VLMs:
- GPT-6 Astra/Sol over-segment (~22 segments/clip vs. 13.8 human mean), collapsing precision (~39%) and strict Boundary F1 (<20%).

title:
The injustice didn’t end with a wrong accusation. It got worse when fighting it became unaffordable.

Lee Castleton face
title_zh: 不公正并没有以错误的指控结束。 当战斗变得负担不起时，情况变得更糟。 Lee Castleton面临着他没有造成的大约23,000 £的缺口。 邮局起诉他
quote_zh: 不公正并没有以错误的指控结束。 当战斗变得负担不起时，情况变得更糟。 Lee Castleton面临着他没有造成的大约23,000 £的缺口。 邮局起诉他
full_text_en:
The injustice didn’t end with a wrong accusation. It got worse when fighting it became unaffordable.

Lee Castleton faced a shortfall of about £23,000 that he hadn’t caused. The Post Office sued him over figures produced by its Horizon system. Unable to afford a lawyer, he represented himself. In 2007, he was ordered to pay £321,000 in legal costs. He went bankrupt. Horizon was later shown to produce false shortfalls.

That case exposes a problem bigger than one faulty system: a right to challenge a decision means little if exercising it can financially ruin you.

Now take that problem into an economy where AI agents will make millions of deals. When a task is disputed or delivery fails to meet agreed terms, someone must assess the evidence and decide what should happen next. If resolving a small claim costs more than the amount at stake, the practical outcome is often that nobody challenges the loss.

@GenLayer is building an adjudication layer for this emerging economy. Independent AI validators review evidence and reach a collective verdict in minutes, at a fraction of the cost of a traditional court.

Speed makes that possible at scale. Trust depends on something harder: validators must assess the evidence independently, and the process must account for decisions that get it wrong.

For AI agent disputes, should a verdict depend primarily on the terms agreed before execution, proof of what actually happened, or whether the evidence satisfies both?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade
full_text_zh:
不公正并没有以错误的指控结束。

当战斗变得难以承受时，情况变得更糟。

李·卡斯尔顿 (Lee Castleton) 面临着约 23,000 英镑的缺口，这并非他造成的。

邮局因其地平线系统生成的数据而起诉他。

由于请不起律师，他为自己辩护。

2007年，他被责令支付321,000英镑的法律费用。

他破产了。

Horizo​​n 后来被证明会产生虚假的短缺。

这个案例暴露了一个比一个有缺陷的系统更大的问题：如果行使质疑一项决定的权利会在经济上毁掉你，那么质疑这一决定的权利就没有什么意义。

现在，将这个问题带入一个人工智能代理将完成数百万笔交易的经济中。

当任务有争议或交付未能满足商定的条件时，必须有人评估证据并决定下一步应该发生什么。

如果解决小额索赔的成本高于所涉金额，则实际结果通常是没有人对损失提出质疑。

@GenLayer

正在为这个新兴经济体建立一个裁决层。

独立的人工智能验证者审查证据并在几分钟内达成集体裁决，而成本只是传统法院的一小部分。

速度使这一切成为可能。

信任取决于更困难的事情：验证者必须独立评估证据，并且该过程必须考虑到错误的决策。

对于人工智能代理纠纷，判决应该主要取决于执行前约定的条款、实际发生情况的证据，还是证据是否满足两者？

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

full_text_en:
The detail worth sitting with is who approves the work when a machine is paying.

An AI agent can post a bounty on @vangrid_io with one HTTP call, fund it in USDC on Base or Arc through x402, and wait. No account, no API key. A contributor walks to the location, captures it, submits. The agent reviews and accepts. Escrow releases on-chain, reconstruction comes back through the same API .

But here's the asymmetry the docs are honest about: spend caps constrain signing. They don't constrain the two calls that matter most. Accepting a submission releases the escrow. Cancelling a bounty ends it. Both irreversible. Both outside the caps .

So the guidance to operators is blunt. Gate those two calls behind human approval when the agent is unattended .

The employer can be software. The approval gate doesn't disappear. It moves. Somewhere between an autonomous agent and a person with a phone, there's still a human deciding whether the work was good enough.

That's the part nobody's pricing in yet. The capture layer is decentralized. The judgment layer isn't.

https://t.co/4ujeHAZcRG
full_text_zh:
值得关注的细节是，当机器付款时，谁批准这项工作。

AI 代理可以通过一次 HTTP 调用在 @vangrid_io 上发布赏金，通过 x402 在 Base 或 Arc 上以 USDC 提供资金，然后等待。没有帐户，没有 API 密钥。贡献者走到该位置，捕获它，然后提交。代理审核并接受。托管在链上发布，重构通过相同的 API 返回。

但文档诚实地指出了不对称性：支出上限限制了签名。它们不会限制最重要的两个调用。接受提交即解除托管。取消赏金就结束了。两者不可逆转。均在瓶盖外。

所以对运营商的指导是生硬的。当客服人员无人值守时，请在人工批准后关闭这两个呼叫。

雇主可以是软件。批准门并没有消失。它移动了。在自主代理和拥有电话的人之间的某个地方，仍然有人决定工作是否足够好。

这是尚未有人定价的部分。捕获层是分散的。判断层则不然。

It answered

full_text_en:
Imagine waking up one morning to find that an AI agent has been running your small online store overnight.

It answered customer requests, researched suppliers, compared prices, and negotiated a purchase while you slept.

Sounds great, right?

But when the supplier asks for payment, a new problem appears. How do you know the agent followed your instructions? What happens if the other party fails to deliver?

This is the part of the agent economy that deserves more attention.

Through @termix_ai, I see an interesting attempt to make interactions between autonomous agents more practical.

https://t.co/5ApLZOsaaq provides a place for agents to be discovered, while AACP helps structure transactions between parties.

The exciting possibility isn’t simply having AI work while we sleep.

It’s building a world where we can confidently delegate real responsibilities to machines.

That’s when autonomous agents start becoming genuinely useful.
full_text_zh:
想象一下，有一天早上醒来，发现人工智能代理已经在运营您的小型在线商店一整夜。

它会在您睡觉时回答客户请求、研究供应商、比较价格并协商购买事宜。

听起来不错，对吧？

但当供应商要求付款时，新的问题又出现了。您如何知道代理遵循了您的指示？如果对方未能交货怎么办？

这是代理经济中值得更多关注的部分。

通过@termix_ai，我看到了一个有趣的尝试，使自主代理之间的交互更加实用。

为代理提供了一个被发现的地方，而 AACP 则帮助构建各方之间的交易。

令人兴奋的可能性不仅仅是让人工智能在我们睡觉时工作。

它正在建设一个我们可以自信地将真正的责任委托给机器的世界。

那时自主代理开始变得真正有用​​。

quote_zh: 我认为物理AI中更重要的转变之一是，请求空间数据的客户可能不再需要是人。 人工智能代理已经可以协调数字任务，但它不能
full_text_en:
I think one of the more important shifts in Physical AI is that the customer requesting spatial data may no longer need to be a person.

An AI agent can already coordinate digital tasks, but it cannot physically inspect a stockroom,walk through a warehouse or record a narrow passage that has changed since the last map was made.

That leaves a gap between what an agent can decide and what it can actually know about a place.

What caught my attention about @vangrid_io is its move toward letting agents request physical world data through an API. An agent can specify a location,set a bounty in USDC and submit the request through the supported payment flow. A human contributor can then capture the site using a smartphone, with accepted work progressing toward a 3D reconstruction.

I find that connection interesting because the agent does not need to own mapping equipment or organise a field team itself. It can initiate the request while people provide the physical access and observation that software cannot supply on its own.

The verification and payment process matters here too. Capture records can be checked against onchain attestations, while bounty terms connect payment to the acceptance process.

This does not mean every request will produce a perfect model or that an agent can operate without human oversight. The quality of the capture and the usefulness of the reconstruction still matter.

But it opens up a different way to think about spatial data. Instead of treating real world mapping as a task that must be planned entirely by people,software can help request the exact information it needs.

That is a meaningful bridge between autonomous software and the physical world, and @vangrid_io is building toward that connection.
full_text_zh:
我认为物理人工智能更重要的转变之一是请求空间数据的客户可能不再需要是一个人。

人工智能代理已经可以协调数字任务，但它无法实际检查储藏室、穿过仓库或记录自上次绘制地图以来发生变化的狭窄通道。

这使得智能体可以做出的决定与它对某个地点的实际了解之间存在差距。

@vangrid_io 引起我注意的是它允许代理通过 API 请求物理世界数据的举措。代理可以指定位置、在 USDC 中设置赏金并通过支持的支付流程提交请求。然后，人类贡献者可以使用智能手机捕获该地点，并接受接受的工作进行 3D 重建。

我发现这种联系很有趣，因为代理不需要拥有测绘设备或自己组织现场团队。当人们提供软件无法单独提供的物理访问和观察时，它可以发起请求。

验证和付款流程在这里也很重要。捕获记录可以根据链上证明进行检查，而赏金条款则将付款与接受过程联系起来。

这并不意味着每个请求都会产生完美的模型，或者代理可以在没有人工监督的情况下运行。捕获的质量和重建的实用性仍然很重要。

但它开辟了一种思考空间数据的不同方式。软件可以帮助请求所需的确切信息，而不是将现实世界的地图视为必须完全由人们规划的任务。

这是自治软件和物理世界之间一座有意义的桥梁，@vangrid_io 正在建立这种连接。

full_text_en:
Friends, good morning.

We need to note the difference before moving forward.

Posting a job will never lock the deal, but accepting an offer and funding it gonna move the transaction forward.

The funniest thing is that with @termix_ai, the buyer journey looks simple and straightforward:

📍Publish: 

You only need to post a request on agent. family with a clear brief and budget range. After this, Providers discover it and submit offers. The terms are still open, and no on-chain order exists yet.

📍Accept:

You have to choose an offer. So, the agreed terms are ready to become the basis of the order, but funding is the key next step.

📍Fund:

The Checkout will send the agreed payment into the TermixEscrow contract. Once funding succeeds, the on-chain order moves to FUNDED / IN_PROGRESS. The terms are locked, and the provider’s required stake is locked for the job.

📍Deliver:

The Funds will remain in escrow while the job progresses through delivery, one redo, a challenge, or a permissionless timeout under the protocol’s rules.

This is very important because the platform does not simply hold the payment alone; the smart contract also governs its release according to the order lifecycle. That gives both sides a defined process from funding to settlement.

I wanna ask: how much does verifiable escrow influence your trust when hiring an AI agent?

📍发布：

您只需向代理提出请求即可。家庭有明确的简介和预算范围。此后，提供商发现它并提交报价。条款仍处于开放状态，尚不存在链上订单。

📍接受：

您必须选择一个报价。因此，商定的条款已准备好成为订单的基础，但资金是下一步的关键。

📍基金：

Checkout 会将商定的付款发送到 TermixEscrow 合约中。一旦融资成功，链上订单就会转为 FUNDED / IN_PROGRESS。条款已锁定，并且提供商所需的股份也已锁定。

📍交付：

根据协议规则，在工作通过交付、一次重做、挑战或未经许可的超时进行过程中，资金将继续托管。

这一点非常重要，因为平台不只是简单地单独持有支付；智能合约还根据订单生命周期管理其发布。这为双方提供了从融资到结算的明确流程。

Where should your AI agent run untrusted code?

An AI agent needs a workspace to run commands, install tools, and save files while completing a task.

It may also generate code or download it from external sources. 

We should treat it as untrusted code and run it in an isolated workspace with limited access.

This is where Kubernetes Agent Sandbox comes in.

In our recent newsletter, we covered the following

- Why AI agents need an isolated workspace to run untrusted code 
- How Kubernetes Agent Sandbox manages these workspaces
- How gVisor and Kata Containers isolate agent workloads
- Hands-on: Deploy a Kubernetes troubleshooting agent and run untrusted code

and more..

title_zh:

quote_zh: 自动化造成了一个奇怪的问责缺口：人工智能代理可以在没有人类做出每一个决定的情况下执行协议，但当协议出错时，仍然有人要承担后果。 想象一个代理选择一个供应商，接受货物，然后付款。如果供应商失败
full_text_en:
Automation creates a strange accountability gap: an AI agent can execute an agreement without a human making each decision, but someone still bears the consequences when that agreement goes wrong.

Imagine an agent choosing a supplier, accepting a delivery, and releasing payment. If the supplier fails to meet the terms, the dispute may involve several automated decisions rather than one obvious point of failure.

Blaming the last agent in the chain won't necessarily explain what went wrong. The parties need a way to examine the actual agreement and the evidence behind competing claims.

That's why @GenLayer's adjudication layer matters to the agent economy. Multiple independent AI validators review evidence and reach a collective verdict in minutes, at a fraction of the cost of a court.

Faster execution is useful. Knowing how disagreements will be resolved is what makes autonomous commerce more practical.

Who should bear responsibility when several agents contribute to the same failed transaction?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade
full_text_zh:
自动化造成了一个奇怪的责任差距：人工智能代理可以在没有人类做出每个决定的情况下执行协议，但当协议出错时，仍然有人要承担后果。

想象一下代理选择供应商、接受交货并发放付款。如果供应商未能满足条款，争议可能涉及多项自动决策，而不是一个明显的故障点。

责怪链条中的最后一个代理人并不能解释到底出了什么问题。双方需要一种方法来审查实际协议和相互竞争的主张背后的证据。

这就是为什么@GenLayer 的裁决层对代理经济很重要。多个独立的人工智能验证者审查证据并在几分钟内达成集体裁决，而费用只是法庭的一小部分。

更快的执行速度很有用。了解如何解决分歧使得自主商业更加实用。

当多个代理促成同一笔交易失败时，谁应该承担责任？

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

full_text_en:
The smallest disputes may become the biggest blind spot in an automated economy.

If an AI agent loses $8 on a disputed transaction, spending hours and significant fees to recover it makes little economic sense. The rational choice may be to accept the loss, even when the claim is legitimate.

Now multiply that decision across millions of deals. A process that makes individual disputes too expensive to pursue could quietly shift costs onto users and businesses, without any single incident looking serious enough to fix.

This is where @GenLayer's focus on faster, lower-cost adjudication becomes relevant. Its model uses multiple independent AI validators to review evidence and reach a collective verdict in minutes, at a fraction of the cost of a court.

But affordability has to work for both sides, and the process still needs reliable evidence.

If resolving a dispute costs more than the amount at stake, who ultimately pays for that inefficiency?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade
full_text_zh:
在自动化经济中，最小的争议可能会成为最大的盲点。

如果人工智能代理在有争议的交易中损失了 8 美元，那么花费大量时间和大量费用来挽回损失就没有什么经济意义。

理性的选择可能是接受损失，即使索赔是合法的。

现在，将这一决策应用到数百万笔交易中。

如果一个流程使得个别纠纷的成本过高而无法解决，那么可能会悄悄地将成本转移到用户和企业身上，而不会出现任何看起来严重到需要解决的单一事件。

这就是 @GenLayer

但负担能力必须对双方都有好处，而且这个过程仍然需要可靠的证据。

如果解决纠纷的成本超过了所涉金额，那么最终谁会为这种低效率买单？

full_text_en:
I tested @evermind’s EverOS Cloud by giving an AI agent something important to remember: a project decision.

For my fictional SpendWise app, I saved:
→ PostgreSQL as the database
→ Infrastructure budget under $100/month
→ A managed database at ~$180/month rejected for exceeding the budget
→ Reconsider only if traffic or operational needs justify the cost

Then I opened a fresh session and searched EverOS for that decision. It retrieved the saved episode and profile, and the next-step recommendation respected those constraints, without resending the original decision.

That’s persistent memory in action: save context once, retrieve it later, and use it to inform the next task.
full_text_zh:
我测试了 @evermind

的 EverOS Cloud，为 AI 代理提供了一些需要记住的重要信息：项目决策。

对于我虚构的 SpendWise 应用程序，我保存了：
→ PostgreSQL 作为数据库
→ 基础设施预算低于 100 美元/月
→ 托管数据库的价格约为 180 美元/月，因超出预算而被拒绝
→ 仅当流量或运营需求证明成本合理时才重新考虑 然后我打开了一个新的会话，并在 EverOS 中搜索了这个决定。

它检索已保存的剧集和个人资料，下一步推荐会尊重这些限制，而无需重新发送原始决策。

这就是持久内存的作用：保存一次上下文，稍后检索它，并用它来通知下一个任务。

full_text_en:
GM gVAN 

Ground truth often takes weeks to arrive.

Here is what it takes to learn what one specific place looks like today:

→ Mapping van: schedule a route, wait for the drive, then wait for processing
→ Sensor box: design it, manufacture it, ship it, book an installer, and hope the density shows up
→ A phone: already in someone's pocket near the place, on a street they walk every day

@vangrid_io is built on the third option. It is a DePIN for spatial data where the node is the device a contributor already carries, so there is no unit to build, no pallet to track, and no installer to schedule. A requester names a place and funds a bounty in USDC. Someone nearby opens the app and walks a slow orbit, and a preview comes back first so a weak pass gets caught before the full 3D reconstruction. Faces and license plates are blurred on the device, each capture is fingerprinted at record time, and the batch is anchored on Base through EAS so the origin can be verified onchain.

The requester can also be software. An AI agent can book a flight and file an invoice, but it cannot walk a loading bay. Through Vangrid's bounty API, the agent posts a job with one HTTP call, pays in USDC through x402 on Base or Arc, and a person nearby takes the work. Funds sit in escrow until the agent accepts a submission, and they return in full if the job is cancelled or the deadline passes. On Arc, settlement finalizes in under a second. No crew to email and no invoice to chase.

For Physical AI, that changes the question from "how long until we get data?" to "who is standing near the place right now?"

If your robot or agent needed a place it has never seen by Friday, which would you rather wait for: a crew, a unit, or a person with a phone?
full_text_zh:
通用汽车货车 事实真相通常需要几周的时间才能到达。

要了解某个特定地点今天的面貌，需要执行以下操作：
→ 测绘车：安排路线，等待开车，然后等待处理
→ 传感器盒：设计、制造、运输、预订安装人员，并希望密度能够显示出来
→ 一部手机：已经在附近某个人的口袋里，在他们每天走过的街道上 @vangrid_io

是基于第三个选项构建的。

它是空间数据的 DePIN，其中节点是贡献者已经携带的设备，因此无需构建单元，无需跟踪托盘，也无需安排安装人员。

请求者指定一个地点并以 USDC 提供赏金。

附近的人打开应用程序并在缓慢的轨道上行走，预览会首先返回，因此在完整的 3D 重建之前会捕获较弱的通道。

设备上的人脸和车牌都是模糊的，每次捕获都会在记录时间进行指纹识别，并且批次通过 EAS 锚定在 Base 上，因此可以在链上验证来源。

请求者也可以是软件。

人工智能代理可以预订航班并提交发票，但无法在装货区行走。

通过 Vangrid 的赏金 API，代理通过一次 HTTP 调用发布一份工作，通过 Base 或 Arc 上的 x402 以 USDC 支付，然后附近的人接手该工作。

在代理商接受提交之前，资金将被托管，如果工作被取消或截止日期已过，资金将全额返还。

在 Arc 上，结算会在不到一秒的时间内完成。

无需向工作人员发送电子邮件，也无需追索发票。

对于物理人工智能来说，这改变了“我们需要多长时间才能获得数据？

”的问题。

到“现在谁站在这个地方附近？

” 如果你的机器人或代理人需要一个它在周五之前从未见过的地方，你宁愿等待哪一个：一个工作人员、一个单位，还是一个有电话的人？

AI is no longer just about generating answers.

It's also about planning tasks, making decisions, using tools, and taking action.

But these three concepts are not the same.

🔹 𝗚𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗔𝗜

Creates new content such as text, images, code, and videos based on user prompts.

Examples: ChatGPT, DALL·E.

🔹 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗔𝗜

Focuses on achieving a goal by planning steps, using tools, evaluating progress, and adjusting its approach when needed.

Think of it as AI that can work through a task instead of simply responding to a prompt.

🔹 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀

These are systems that can observe information, make decisions, and take actions toward a specific goal with varying levels of autonomy.

For example, an AI agent could search for information, interact with APIs, complete a workflow, and check the results.

𝗛𝗲𝗿𝗲'𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲 𝗱𝗶𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲:

→ Generative AI creates.
→ Agentic AI plans and works toward goals.
→ AI agents execute tasks and interact with their environment.

These concepts can overlap. An AI agent can use a generative AI model, while agentic AI describes the broader approach to goal-oriented action.

Understanding the difference helps you see where AI is heading: beyond generating content toward completing useful work.

quote_zh: 如果你学习人工智能安全工程，你将永远不会再失业。 阶段1 ：威胁建模和基础 -学习： OWASP LLM前10名、MITRE ATLAS、STRIDE、信任边界。 -练习：四
full_text_en:
If you learn AI Security Engineering, you will never be unemployed again.

Stage 1: Threat Modeling & Foundations
- Learn: OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, MITRE ATLAS, STRIDE, trust boundaries.

- Practice: Threat model a RAG chatbot and map every place untrusted text enters the system.

Stage 2: Prompt Injection & Jailbreaks
- Learn: Direct vs indirect injection, instruction hierarchy, multi-turn attacks.

- Practice: Hijack a sandboxed agent with a poisoned webpage, then patch it.

Stage 3: Insecure Output Handling
- Learn: LLM-driven XSS, SQLi, SSRF, command injection, excessive agency.

- Practice: Exploit an app that pipes model output into a shell, then fix it with strict validation.

Stage 4: RAG & Vector DB Security
- Learn: Embedding poisoning, tenant isolation, ACL-aware retrieval.

- Practice: Plant a malicious document in a knowledge base and make the bot leak another user's data.

Stage 5: Agent & Tool Security
- Learn: Least privilege, confused deputy attacks, sandboxing, scoped credentials.

- Practice: Give an agent shell and email tools, then build a permission layer that blocks dangerous chains.

Stage 6: MCP Security
- Learn: Tool poisoning, rug pulls, tool shadowing, OAuth scopes, server authentication.

- Practice: Build a malicious MCP server that exfiltrates data, then write a scanner that catches it.

Stage 7: Data Leakage & Privacy
- Learn: PII exposure, training data extraction, membership inference, DLP.

- Practice: Extract memorized strings from a fine-tuned model and measure the leakage rate.

Stage 8: Model Supply Chain
- Learn: Pickle deserialization, safetensors, model signing, AI-BOM, typosquatting.

- Practice: Craft a malicious model file that executes code on load, then build a pipeline that refuses it.

Stage 9: Adversarial ML
- Learn: Evasion, data poisoning, backdoors, model extraction.

- Practice: Backdoor a small classifier with 1% poisoned data and detect it afterward.

Stage 10: Guardrails & Runtime Enforcement
- Learn: Input/output classifiers, policy engines, deterministic checks, human-in-the-loop.

- Practice: Put a policy gateway in front of an agent that blocks risky actions before they execute.

Stage 11: Red Teaming & Evals
- Learn: garak, PyRIT, promptfoo, attack success rate, regression suites.

- Practice: Automate a red-team pipeline in CI that fails the build when a new jailbreak lands.

Stage 12: Detection, IR & Governance
- Learn: Audit logging, anomaly detection, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, EU AI Act.

- Practice: Write an incident response playbook for a compromised agent, then run a tabletop exercise.

Chatbots are a commodity. AI Security is the physics of trust.

The modern AI Security Engineer builds the immune system for autonomous intelligence.

Bookmark and Repost!
full_text_zh:
如果你学了人工智能安全工程，你就再也不会失业了。

第一阶段：威胁建模和基础
- 学习：法学硕士 OWASP 前 10 名、MITRE ATLAS、STRIDE、信任边界。

- 练习：对 RAG 聊天机器人进行威胁建模，并映射不受信任的文本进入系统的每个位置。

第二阶段：快速注射和越狱
- 学习：直接注入与间接注入、指令层次结构、多轮攻击。

- 练习：用中毒网页劫持沙盒代理，然后修补它。

第三阶段：不安全的输出处理
- 学习：LLM驱动的XSS、SQLi、SSRF、命令注入、过度代理。

- 实践：利用一个将模型输出传输到 shell 的应用程序，然后通过严格的验证来修复它。

第 4 阶段：RAG 和矢量数据库安全
- 学习：嵌入中毒、租户隔离、ACL 感知检索。

- 实践：在知识库中植入恶意文档，使机器人泄露其他用户的数据。

第五阶段：代理和工具安全
- 学习：最小特权、混乱的代理攻击、沙箱、范围凭证。

- 实践：提供代理外壳和电子邮件工具，然后构建阻止危险链的权限层。

第 6 阶段：MCP 安全
- 学习：工具中毒、地毯拉扯、工具影子、OAuth 范围、服务器身份验证。

- 实践：构建一个恶意 MCP 服务器来窃取数据，然后编写一个扫描程序来捕获数据。

第七阶段：数据泄露和隐私
- 学习：PII 暴露、训练数据提取、成员资格推断、DLP。

- 练习：从微调模型中提取记忆的字符串并测量泄漏率。

第八阶段：供应链模型
- 学习：Pickle 反序列化、安全张量、模型签名、AI-BOM、拼写错误。

- 实践：制作一个在加载时执行代码的恶意模型文件，然后构建一个拒绝它的管道。

第 9 阶段：对抗性机器学习
- 学习：规避、数据中毒、后门、模型提取。

- 练习：用1%的中毒数据对一个小分类器进行后门，然后进行检测。

第 10 阶段：护栏和运行时执行
- 学习：输入/输出分类器、策略引擎、确定性检查、人机交互。

- 实践：在代理前面放置一个策略网关，在危险操作执行之前阻止它们。

第 11 阶段：红队和评估
- 学习：garak、PyRIT、promptfoo、攻击成功率、回归套件。

- 实践：自动化 CI 中的红队管道，该管道在新越狱登陆时构建失败。

第 12 阶段：检测、IR 和治理
- 学习：审核日志记录、异常检测、NIST AI RMF、ISO 42001、欧盟 AI 法案。

- 练习：为受感染的代理编写事件响应手册，然后进行桌面练习。

聊天机器人是一种商品。

人工智能安全是信任的物理原理。

现代人工智能安全工程师为自主智能构建免疫系统。

full_text_en:
GLM 5.4/ GLM 5.5 on the way... ZCode just got what might be its biggest update yet with the new Workflow mode, and it feels like a completely different experience! I asked it to orchestrate 10 subagents at once and now I can actually watch each one working independently, see how the tasks are progressing and follow the entire workflow in real time. What I love the most is the interface, everything is so well organized and being able to see exactly what each agent is doing makes the whole experience much better, especially when you're working on complicated projects with multiple agents.

To give you an idea of how Dynamic Workflows works, instead of having an AI agent coordinate everything through chat, you now have code that coordinates the agents directly, which makes managing complex tasks much more structured. And when you combine this with Goal Mode, Execution Modes, support for multiple models and GLM's long context window, ZCode is becoming one of the most advanced tools I've tried in 2026 for large development projects that require multiple agents working together!
full_text_zh:
GLM 5.4/ GLM 5.5 即将推出...ZCode 刚刚获得了可能是其最大的更新，推出了新的工作流程模式，感觉就像是一种完全不同的体验！我要求它同时编排 10 个子代理，现在我实际上可以观察每个子代理的独立工作，了解任务的进展情况并实时跟踪整个工作流程。我最喜欢的是界面，一切都组织得很好，能够准确地看到每个代理正在做什么，使整个体验变得更好，特别是当您与多个代理一起处理复杂的项目时。

为了让您了解动态工作流程的工作原理，您现在不必让 AI 代理通过聊天来协调一切，而是直接协调代理的代码，这使得管理复杂任务更加结构化。当您将其与目标模式、执行模式、对多种模型的支持以及 GLM 的长上下文窗口相结合时，ZCode 正在成为我在 2026 年尝试过的最先进的工具之一，用于需要多个代理协同工作的大型开发项目！

quote_zh: 我们最新的模型进步为用低资源编程语言（如COBOL、Fortran和Visual Basic）构建和迁移软件带来了更强的能力。 这些语言为银行、政府和企业所依赖的软件提供了动力。这里的进步意味着理解几十年的“但是”
full_text_en:
Our latest model advances bring stronger capabilities for building and migrating software in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic.

These languages power software that banks, governments, and businesses depend on. Progress here means understanding decades of business logic and helping developers modernize those systems while preserving what works.

We’re building these capabilities around the challenges developers and enterprise customers bring us. If your team is working on these systems, tell us which languages and workflows we should tackle next.

https://t.co/2TbnkQixJ1
full_text_zh:
我们最新的模型进步带来了使用 COBOL、Fortran 和 Visual Basic 等低资源编程语言构建和迁移软件的更强大功能。

这些语言为银行、政府和企业所依赖的软件提供支持。这里的进步意味着理解数十年的业务逻辑并帮助开发人员实现这些系统的现代化，同时保留有效的内容。

我们正在围绕开发人员和企业客户给我们带来的挑战构建这些功能。如果您的团队正在开发这些系统，请告诉我们下一步应该处理哪些语言和工作流程。

full_text_en:
Claude Code 2.1.304 has been released.

76 CLI changes

Highlights:
• tool.check decider:\"person\" makes a mod require human approval; unapproved asks are refused with mod reason
• Added /auto-mode-setup: guided scan of project and history so Auto Mode learns environment for smarter actions
• Added /claude-api managed-agents-secure: read-only check flags Managed Agents deviations vs Anthropic guide

Full details available in thread ↓
full_text_zh:
Claude Code
2. 1.304 已发布。

76 CLI 更改 亮点：
• tool.check 决策者：\“person\”使 mod 需要人工批准；未经批准的请求会因 mod 原因被拒绝
• 添加了 /auto-mode-setup：引导扫描项目和历史记录，以便自动模式了解环境以进行更智能的操作
• 添加了 /claude-api Managed-agents-secure：只读检查标记 Managed Agents 偏差与 Anthropic 指南 完整详情请参阅线程 ↓

full_text_en:
Opus 5.5 + 15 motion styles = your own f*cking motion studio that runs 24/7

give Claude Code 15 motion design styles, then ask it to turn them into a studio that never stops rendering

how to set it up:

> pick a style and give Claude Code a motion reference: a clip, a gif or a few frames
> ask it to break the motion down: timing, easing, palette, signature moves
> squeeze that into one short prompt: length, format, style, 3 moves, title, music + sfx
> one prompt = one 10s film, visuals and sound all from code
> repeat for all 15 styles and save every prompt as a reusable preset
> put them on one loop: every style gets a live tile, a preview and a copy button

now you don't start from a blank timeline. you pick a style, copy the prompt, swap the title, render

title:
AI will not automate radiologists like you think

We have been talking for years now about AI automating jobs. Radiology
title_zh:
人工智能不会像你想象的那样自动化放射科医生

多年来，我们一直在谈论人工智能自动化工作。 放射学一直是一个主要目标， Geoff Hinton曾经声称， “人们应该停止
quote_zh: 人工智能不会像你想象的那样自动化放射科医生 多年来，我们一直在谈论人工智能自动化工作。 放射学一直是一个主要目标， Geoff Hinton曾经声称， “人们应该停止
full_text_en:
AI will not automate radiologists like you think

We have been talking for years now about AI automating jobs. Radiology has been a prime target, with Geoff Hinton once claiming, “people should stop training radiologists now, it’s just completely obvious that within five years, deep learning is going to do better than radiologists”, which is funny since he said that in 2016. There is now more demand for radiologists than ever, so clearly things did not turn out the way many thought. Here I will make a prediction that while radiology will change in the coming decade, radiologists will not be automated away any time soon. I will use radiology as an example but I think these principles will broadly apply to any field where demand can be elastic and quality can scale with increased intelligence.

First of all, we have seen in the short history of language models that there is a “jagged edge of intelligence”, where AI excels at verifiable tasks with a lot of data but is underwhelming on less common tasks. One thing most AI researchers underestimate about radiology is that it is actually extremely multi-task. There are at least a hundred conditions that can be diagnosed from x-rays alone, and thousands using CT and MRI. AI will first master common and easy-to-see conditions and it will not be as good as experts at less-common diseases just because there is less data for that. This jagged edge will certainly improve over time but this means that AI will certainly be used as a triage tool at first, rather than full automation in one go. I would guess that this process from solid triage tool to full automation would take 3-5 years in the best case scenario, because training AI to get all the edge cases right will be bottlenecked by data collection of rare diseases, and also because radiology isn’t currently a focus for frontier labs.

Second, there will be elastic demand for radiology as it gets cheaper per unit. I think elastic demand (“Jevons paradox”) is the most underrated phenomenon when people think about AI automation. In software, it is obvious that I have way more demand than before because Claude Code makes it so easy. These days I ask Claude Code to build a custom three-thousand line html viewer to help me visualize every little RL run that I do. The same thing will happen in radiology. If there is essentially no cost or latency of interpreting an MRI, a physician can order many scans preemptively to better diagnose a case. So with AI tools, a radiologist might have to read only 20% of inbound scans, but there might be 5x more scans inbound. Many developing countries have fewer than one radiologist per million people and they will also want to send a lot of radiology to be interpreted.

Longer term, cheap and fast radiology interpretation will also drive incentives to build cheaper radiology scanners. If an MRI had essentially no latency for interpretation, medical devices companies will want to build much cheaper MRI machines that can be used more frequently, perhaps even in the middle of a surgery. AI will accelerate the development of scanning technology, too. If a full body MRI was only $100 dollars I would totally want to get one every month instead of every two years. I can imagine a world where people get 10 or 100x the number of scans they do today, largely for preventative care, if radiology were 10-100x cheaper.

Third, even if we did have a model that could outperform the world’s best radiologists today, that would not be the end of all work on radiology. Medicine is a field of change. We may develop new treatment protocols that require reading radiology images in a way that radiologists currently aren’t used to. New scanners may reveal diseases that we cannot currently diagnose today with radiology alone. Some radiologists will change their work from reading scans to doing frontier research to advance our understanding of radiology and translate new knowledge into updated models.

Moreover, I am sure that we will ask for more out of our AI models than ever before. With a good flywheel, we may one day train AI models that can use radiology images to predict disease probabilities far into the future. With good prediction algorithms, cancer may be detected months earlier than we can detect it now. Society will invest a lot into this research and this will contribute even more to increased demand for radiology and the best AI around it.

On top of all of this, the medical system is typically slower to adopt new technology and has more regulation compared to technology companies. There is legacy infrastructure and medical centers need to constantly support patients which makes it hard to integrate new technology. This is even more true in developing countries. Moreover data access tends to be limited due to HIPAA, deidentification, IRBs, etc. So I think radiologists will be in demand for a while.

While some worry about radiology being totally automated, I think there is a more exciting future for radiology than ever before—one where there is more demand and we ask for more predictive power from our intelligence. This is similar to how many of us feel that programming will thrive more than ever before despite drastic change in the field. More generally, any domain where demand can be elastic and quality can scale with increased intelligence will, like radiology, similarly flourish with the development of AI. This is certainly a more exciting and nuanced future than what Hinton described in 2016!

(Finally, to be fair to Hinton, he did acknowledge in a recent podcast that he was wrong and also agrees with the elastic demand argument.)

Thanks @JayRothschild and @engyziedan for feedback on this post.
full_text_zh:
人工智能不会像你想象的那样让放射科医生自动化

多年来我们一直在谈论人工智能自动化工作。放射科一直是首要目标，Geoff Hinton 曾声称，“人们现在应该停止培训放射科医生，很明显，五年之内，深度学习将比放射科医生做得更好”，自从他在 2016 年说这句话以来，这很有趣。现在对放射科医生的需求比以往任何时候都多，所以显然事情并没有像许多人想象的那样。在这里，我将做出一个预测，虽然放射学将在未来十年内发生变化，但放射科医生不会很快被自动化取代。我将以放射学为例，但我认为这些原则将广泛适用于需求具有弹性且质量可以随着智能的提高而扩展的任何领域。

首先，我们在语言模型的短暂历史中看到，存在“智力的锯齿状边缘”，即人工智能擅长处理具有大量数据的可验证任务，但在不太常见的任务上表现不佳。大多数人工智能研究人员低估放射学的一件事是，它实际上是极其多任务的。仅通过 X 射线就可以诊断出至少一百种疾病，而使用 CT 和 MRI 则可以诊断数千种疾病。人工智能将首先掌握常见且易于观察的疾病，并且它不会像不太常见疾病的专家那样擅长，因为这方面的数据较少。这种锯齿状边缘肯定会随着时间的推移而改善，但这意味着人工智能首先肯定会被用作分类工具，而不是一次性完全自动化。我猜想，在最好的情况下，从可靠的分类工具到完全自动化的过程将需要 3-5 年的时间，因为训练人工智能以正确处理所有边缘情况将受到罕见疾病数据收集的瓶颈，而且因为放射学目前不是前沿实验室的重点。

其次，随着单位成本的降低，放射学的需求将会变得富有弹性。我认为，当人们考虑人工智能自动化时，弹性需求（“杰文斯悖论”）是最被低估的现象。在软件方面，很明显我的需求比以前要多得多，因为 Claude Code 让一切变得如此简单。这些天，我要求 Claude Code 构建一个自定义的 3000 行 html 查看器，以帮助我可视化我所做的每一次小型 RL 运行。同样的事情也会发生在放射学领域。如果解读 MRI 基本上没有成本或延迟，医生可以预先安排多次扫描，以更好地诊断病例。因此，使用 AI 工具，放射科医生可能只需读取 20% 的入站扫描，但入站扫描的数量可能会增加 5 倍。许多发展中国家每百万人中只有不到一名放射科医生，他们还希望派出大量放射科人员进行解读。

从长远来看，廉价且快速的放射学解释也将推动建造更便宜的放射学扫描仪的动力。如果 MRI 基本上没有解释延迟，医疗设备公司将希望制造更便宜的 MRI 机器，可以更频繁地使用，甚至可能在手术过程中使用。人工智能也将加速扫描技术的发展。如果全身 MRI 仅需 100 美元，我绝对希望每个月而不是每两年做一次。我可以想象这样一个世界：如果放射学便宜 10 到 100 倍，人们接受的扫描次数将是现在的 10 或 100 倍，主要用于预防性护理。

第三，即使我们确实拥有一个可以超越当今世界上最好的放射科医生的模型，这也不会是所有放射学工作的结束。医学是一个不断变化的领域。我们可能会开发新的治疗方案，需要以放射科医生目前不习惯的方式读取放射图像。新的扫描仪可能会揭示出我们目前仅靠放射学无法诊断的疾病。一些放射科医生会将他们的工作从阅读扫描转变为进行前沿研究，以增进我们对放射学的理解并将新知识转化为更新的模型。

此外，我确信我们对人工智能模型的要求将比以往任何时候都要高。有了一个好的飞轮，有一天我们可能会训练出可以使用放射学图像来预测未来疾病概率的人工智能模型。有了良好的预测算法，癌症可能会比我们现在检测到的时间提前几个月。社会将在这项研究上投入大量资金，这将进一步增加对放射学及其最佳人工智能的需求。

最重要的是，与科技公司相比，医疗系统采用新技术的速度通常较慢，并且受到更多监管。遗留的基础设施和医疗中心需要不断地支持患者，这使得整合新技术变得困难。在发展中国家更是如此。此外，由于 HIPAA、去身份识别、IRB 等原因，数据访问往往受到限制。所以我认为放射科医生将在一段时间内受到需求。

虽然有些人担心放射学完全自动化，但我认为放射学的未来比以往任何时候都更加令人兴奋——需求更多，我们要求我们的情报具有更强的预测能力。这就像我们很多人认为的那样，尽管该领域发生了巨大的变化，但编程将比以往任何时候都更加蓬勃发展。更一般地说，任何需求具有弹性、质量可以随着智能的增加而扩展的领域，就像放射学一样，同样会随着人工智能的发展而蓬勃发展。这无疑是一个比 Hinton 在 2016 年描述的更令人兴奋和微妙的未来！

（最后，公平地说，Hinton 在最近的播客中承认自己错了，并且也同意弹性需求论点。）

感谢 @JayRothschild 和 @engyziedan 对这篇文章的反馈。

title: AI can write code, analyze data, and make decisions. But what happens when it needs to see a building that has changed,
title_zh: 人工智能可以编写代码、分析数据并做出决策。 但是，当它需要看到已经改变的建筑物、检查街道或获得真实地点的全新3D视图时，会发生什么？ 它需要有人在
quote_zh: 人工智能可以编写代码、分析数据并做出决策。 但是，当它需要看到已经改变的建筑物、检查街道或获得真实地点的全新3D视图时，会发生什么？ 它需要有人在
full_text_en:
AI can write code, analyze data, and make decisions. But what happens when it needs to see a building that has changed, inspect a street, or get a fresh 3D view of a real place?

It needs someone on the ground.

That’s what caught my attention about @vangrid_io going live on Arc.

An AI agent can post a USDC bounty, get someone to visit the location and capture the area, then receive a 3D model built from that footage.

No need to send a robot across town. No need to rely on images that might be years old.

A person handles the capture, @vangrid_io turns it into usable spatial data, and the agent gets what it needs to keep working.

Robotics companies could get updated views of their surroundings. AI systems could access real-world information that simply isn't available online. And people with smartphones could earn money by helping these systems see places they cannot reach themselves.

AI still needs the physical world, even if it doesn't have a body.

Now there's a way to connect the two, with humans doing the work and onchain payments handling the reward.

This is one of the reasons I'm watching VanGrid.
full_text_zh:
人工智能可以编写代码、分析数据并做出决策。

但是，当它需要查看发生变化的建筑物、检查街道或获得真实地点的全新 3D 视图时，会发生什么情况呢？

它需要有人在现场。

这就是 @vangrid_io

在 Arc 上上线引起我注意的原因。

title:
THIS IS STUPIDLY F*CKING GOLD

7 raw inputs. 7 compilers. 50 of 50 sources fed into one linked wiki. This Opus 5.5 board
title_zh:
这是愚蠢的他妈的黄金

7个原始输入。7个编译器。50个源中的50个输入到一个链接的wiki中。 这款Opus 5.5板有一个几乎没有人使用的笔记技巧。

理念：停止将笔记存储在7个分隔符中
quote_zh: 这是愚蠢的他妈的黄金 7个原始输入。7个编译器。50个源中的50个输入到一个链接的wiki中。 这款Opus 5.5板有一个几乎没有人使用的笔记技巧。 理念：停止将笔记存储在7个分隔符中
full_text_en:
THIS IS STUPIDLY F*CKING GOLD

7 raw inputs. 7 compilers. 50 of 50 sources fed into one linked wiki. This Opus 5.5 board has a notes trick almost nobody uses.

The idea: stop storing notes in 7 separate piles. Every pile goes through its own compiler and comes out as linked knowledge. The counter starts at 9 of 50, and the owl only finishes when it hits 50.

No forgotten Claude Code sessions, no unread raw notes, and you can see which source feeds which part of the wiki.

The whole pipeline is one line:
sources → compiler → owl

here's the split:
→ code, docs and SQL go into graphify, a queryable knowledge graph
→ a whole project goes into Understand-Anything, a graph you learn from your codebase
→ sources you read once go into claude-obsidian, grounded answers
→ Claude Code sessions go into obsidian-second-brain, plain markdown memory
→ your chats go into claude-code-memory-setup, vault plus code graphs
→ raw notes go into second-brain, maintained by the LLM
→ collected files go into llm-wikid, cross-linked wiki pages

You only look at three moments:
→ 9 of 50 fed: the owl is a few loose blocks
→ 36 of 50: the shape is there, still full of holes
→ 50 of 50: compiled wiki, linked

↳ the footer says it straight: the compiler is not the brain, the brain is what you feed it
full_text_zh:
这真是愚蠢的黄金 7 个原始输入。

7 个编译器。

50 个来源中的 50 个被输入到一个链接的 wiki 中。

这款 Opus
5. 5 开发板有一个几乎没人使用的笔记技巧。

这个想法是：停止将笔记分成七堆。

每堆都经过自己的编译器并作为链接的知识出现。

计数器从 50 中的 9 开始，猫头鹰只有在达到 50 时才结束。

没有被遗忘的 Claude Code 会议，没有未读的原始笔记，您可以看到哪个源提供了 wiki 的哪个部分。

整个管道是一行：
来源
→ 编译器
→ owl 这是分裂：
→ 代码、文档和 SQL 进入可查询的知识图谱 graphify
→ 整个项目进入 Understanding-Anything，这是您从代码库中学到的图表
→ 你读过的资源进入了克劳德·黑曜石，扎根的答案
→ Claude Code 会话进入黑曜石第二大脑、纯 Markdown 内存
→ 你的聊天内容会进入 claude-code-memory-setup、vault plus 代码图
→ 原始笔记进入第二大脑，由法学硕士维护
→ 收集的文件进入 llm-wikid、交叉链接的 wiki 页面 你只看三个时刻：
→ 50 喂食中的 9 只：猫头鹰是一些松散的方块
→ 50 中的 36：形状就在那里，但仍然布满孔洞
→ 50 of 50：编译维基，链接 ↳ 页脚直接说：编译器不是大脑，大脑是你喂它的东西

full_text_en:
Claude Code just found a hidden camera in my Airbnb. In the smoke detector…

Checked into one of those $60 Airbnbs where the microwave sits on top of the fridge. Opened Claude Code and asked what else is on this Wi-Fi

It listed everything on the router. All of it was the usual stuff except one box made by a company that only makes CCTV cameras, quietly sending video out of the room every 4 seconds

Claude sent it the "find me" ping installers use. The smoke detector above the bed beeped for 5 seconds and its red recording light came on

The check takes 2 minutes:

step 1 → join the Wi-Fi, open Claude Code, paste the prompt from the first comment

step 2 → it lists every device and flags anything that looks like a camera or a mic

step 3 → if it flags one, turn the lights off and shine your phone flashlight at smoke detectors, clocks and chargers. A lens glints back

You won't remember this at 1am in a strange room. Save it now, thank me on your next trip

Every week I point Claude Code at something in my life and post what it finds. Follow if you want the next one

Ever found one? What did you use to check?
full_text_zh:
Claude Code 刚刚在我的 Airbnb 中发现了一个隐藏的摄像头。

在烟雾探测器中... 入住了其中一间 60 美元的 Airbnb，微波炉位于冰箱顶部。

打开 Claude Code 并询问此 Wi-Fi 上还有什么 它列出了路由器上的所有内容。

所有的东西都是平常的东西，除了一个由一家只生产闭路电视摄像机的公司制造的盒子，每 4 秒悄悄地将视频发送到房间外 克劳德向它发送了“找到我”ping 安装程序使用的信息。

床头烟雾探测器鸣响5秒，红色录音灯亮起 检查需要2分钟：
步骤1→加入Wi-Fi，打开Claude Code，粘贴第一条评论的提示 步骤 2
→ 它列出了所有设备并标记了任何看起来像相机或麦克风的设备 步骤 3
→ 如果有标记，请关闭灯并将手机手电筒照射烟雾探测器、时钟和充电器。

镜头一闪而过 你不会记得凌晨 1 点在一个陌生的房间里发生的事情。

立即保存，下次旅行时感谢我 每周我都会向 Claude Code 指出我生活中的一些事情并发布它的发现。
